Cause (UI, rb485/rb524): those Sprites lacked the libzstd-dev package. `work run` provisions from `$sprite_packages`, read from the CALLER'S checkout (tools/sprite-lib.sh), so a lane branched before #991 added libzstd-dev never asked for it, and `work sprites` judged health by the same stale list, so the box read 'ok'. body:
main's gate is red in `wasm-check` on three disagreements since #1026: `cancel` and `stack` print NOTHING under wasm, and `stack_overflow` ends with status 3 where native ends 2 (job 117929015138, dispatch run 39212407996).

## Cause

The gate runs `wasm-check.sh` under the image's own `node` (22). The hosted scheduler suspends through `WebAssembly.Suspending`, which only a Node 24 has; the image carries one as `node-jspi` (#1005) and `wasm-host-check.sh` already preferred it, but `wasm-check.sh` and `wasm-tasks-mutations.sh` kept `node=${NODE:-node}`. A module that parks printed nothing, and the host's own refusal (`wasm-node.mjs`, exit 3) went to a `.err` file nobody printed.

Reproduced on a Sprite in the gate's state (compiler only, a downloaded Node 22 first on `PATH`): the old script prints exactly the gate's three failures. With `.github/ci/install_node.sh` run (so `node-jspi` is Node 24.18.0) and Node 22 still first on `PATH`, the fixed script prints `wasm-check: all fixtures agree` (cancel, loop, stack, struct, tasks agree; stack_overflow's eval refuses and native, wasm and the fallback end 2 saying `a task's stack overflowed`).

## Fix

- `tools/jspi_node.sh`: one resolver, sourced by `wasm-check`, `wasm-tasks-mutations` and `wasm-host-check` (the last held its own copy of the refusal). It answers `$NODE`, else `node-jspi`, else `node`, and REFUSES a node without `WebAssembly.Suspending` by name ("… install a Node 24 as node-jspi (.github/ci/install_node.sh) or set NODE"), so a wrong environment says what it is instead of printing nothing. No node at all stays the script's own skip.
- `wasm-check` prints the host's stderr when a wasm run differs; `wasm-node.mjs` says what a Node 22 lacks and what to run it under (its old message pointed at a flag that does not give a Node 22 the standard API).
- The PR gap: `gate_changed --pr-minimum` skipped the whole wasm proof, so a PR that changed the wasm fixtures or scripts never ran it and main's gate was the first to see it. It now runs the proof when the PR changes `tools/wasm*`, `tools/jspi_node.sh`, the wasm port's runtime files (`runtime/avra_fiber`, `runtime/dom/tasks*`, `runtime/*wasm*`) or `.github/ci/install_node.sh`.

## Not done

The PR-route rule is a path list in `gate_changed.sh`; if ci-design wants it in checks.yml's path gate instead, that is theirs to move. I have not run `wasm-tasks-mutations` or `wasm-host-check` through the new resolver on a Sprite yet.

body:
## Cause
`core.Children.derive` over Expr settled at 2.15 MB normally and was cut off at **5,246,307 bytes after 65,472 of 99,734 steps** in the failing process (budget 5,242,880). With `[lifted] memory = 64` the same run billed **5,589,624** bytes: 3.4 MB of memory the run did not make. It comes from `type_named`, which asks the workspace from inside the run; the types/signatures the workspace builds to answer stay and were counted against the run (`avra_mem_live() - mem_base`). More compiler state loaded before the derive (a big restored store, a whole-directory suite) means more ambient growth, so the same derive passes on main's push run and fails on a PR's.
The cut was SILENT: a run cut inside a re-entrant expansion is hushed, its declarations are simply absent, and the only symptom is `SyntaxArena has no method expr_children` at every use (7 sites, seen on #916 and #976).

## Reproduction
Downloaded run 39148755475's `avra-compiler` and `avra-build` artifacts, unpacked them over a copy of #976's tree on a Sprite, and ran the failing job's groups in its order (std-derive … std-http, then std-avrac/src/compiler): reproduces (21 `expr_children` errors, rc 1) and is deterministic on the resulting store. The compiler group alone on the fresh artifact store passed. Same run with the fix compiled in: Children settles at 1,273,528 bytes and the compile goes through.

## Fix
`Machine.named_unbilled`: the workspace's answer moves `mem_base` by what it allocated; the answer crossing into the run (`val_of`) is still billed.

## Witness
`compiler/tests/settle_bill_test.av`: a settlement asks a workspace that keeps 4 MiB of what it builds, under a 1 MiB budget. Before: `budget: held more than 1048576 bytes` (1/2 passed). After: 2/2.

## Follow-up (1): a cut derive speaks every time (in this PR)
Why it was silent: the first ask of a refused lift speaks and holds `Refused`; any later ask answers `Spoken` (silent, "the first spoke"), but an expansion's voices are wiped each time its file expands again (`hush_expansion`). So the second expansion read the held refusal, said nothing, and the derive's declarations were absent. `Workspace.lift_refusal` returns the held refusal and the expansion speaks it again (`speak_expansion` dedupes). Witness `compiler/tests/silent_cut_test.av`: a derive over a 1 MiB budget; second expansion (Expanded evicted) was silent before (1/2), speaks after (2/2).

## Follow-up (2): is the bill still a global-heap measure? (scoped, not done)
The run's own allocations can be named at the source only for the callbacks into the compiler, and those are two: `named` (`type_named`, builds kept state — now unbilled) and `embed` (returns the file's bytes: the run's own data, correctly billed). Nothing else reaches compiler state from inside a run (settlements refuse the world; one thread). So after this PR the process-heap delta IS the run's own growth plus what it caused the runtime's own `once` caches to hold, both legitimately its. A per-run allocator scope (exact owner accounting) needs an owner in the 16-byte box header, i.e. a runtime ABI change and seed rung; I did not do it because nothing now needs it. Say if you want it scoped as a ticket.

CI lesson written into docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md (§6 Known traps), including how to reproduce a PR-route failure from the run's artifacts.

Sprite: check --baseline std-avrac clean, settle_bill_test 2/2.

Stacked on #952 (batch D: the hosted scheduler); retarget to main when it lands.

**Host half (tests 8, 9, 11).** `tasks.enter` gives each host callback a stack of its own and queues entries (serial, as turns); a plain call that parks is refused by the engine and spoken as `a task parked under a host call`; `chooseArtifact` picks `app.wasm` or `app.asyncify.wasm` by what the host can suspend. `tasks_unit_test.js` (12 checks, no module) and `tasks_test.js` (against the `tools/wasm-host` reactor) pin them; removing the entry chain turns two checks red.

**The asyncify fallback.** Built BY DEFAULT for a wasm build whose program runs tasks (it calls a runtime row that may switch a task out, `runs_tasks`); `--no-wasm-fallback` opts out. `build.av` writes `app.asyncify.wasm` beside the binary (asyncify over `avra_host.switch` and `avra_host.idle`, the same feature list as the shrink), keeps it under the binary's key and places it on a warm build; the toolchain mode carries `+fallback`, so a build with and without one never share a kept binary. A program that never parks gets no fallback (asyncify adds scaffolding even with no matching import: 0.9 KB to 2.9 KB on an empty module).

`asyncifyTasks` (runtime/dom/tasks.js) drives it without suspending a stack: a task parks by unwinding its frames into a buffer of its own (`avra_asyncify_buffer`, 256 KiB) and is rewound by calling its top-level export again; the driver is a loop that runs one task until it unwinds or ends, then whichever the scheduler named. `tasks_proxy_test.js` holds JSPI and asyncify to the same interleaving, answer and no stranded task on a freestanding module (8 checks, run on the Mac); `wasm-check` holds every task fixture to the same stdout under the fallback, and `stack_overflow` to the same words and status.

**Measured, and owed.** On real Avra output earlier (fib 35 plus a 1M comprehension, whole-program asyncify, indirect calls conservative): +37-38% size; 1.9x on a path that reaches a park, +12% on one that cannot. `wasm-check` now prints each fixture's clean and asyncified size. The scoped onlylist (the `parks` set from `cancel_reach`) is NOT in: the module is stripped of names, an onlylist needs the C runtime's park-path symbols as well, and asyncify's own reachability already prunes what cannot reach the imports, so the onlylist only removes functions whose indirect calls cannot park. That is worth doing only if CI's sizes say the whole-program build is too large; recorded, not built.

**What**
- Literals: `[a, ..xs, b]` (list; runs of plain elements joined by `concat`, a lone spread is a copy) and `{ ..m, "k": v }` (map; an overwritten key keeps its first place, via the pipeline `Put` sink). Voices `type.spread_list`, `type.spread_map`.
- Patterns: list patterns `[first, ..rest]`, `[..init, last]`, `[a, ..]`, `[]` and record patterns `P { x, y: pat, .. }` (`Pat.Seq`, `Pat.Fields`, owned by lists and structs through the pattern seam); `is` over them in `if`; destructuring `let P { x, y } = p` / `let [a, ..rest] = xs else { … }` as a `LetPattern` node whose meaning (the match) is minted through the means door — no mark, the printer reads the node. A head-and-tail match is exhaustive. `destructure` is a grammar seam (`Grammar.with_seam`, declared in stmt_spine). Voices `type.list_pattern`, `type.record_pattern`, `type.let_pattern`. Retires the subset-today entry on struct destructuring in `let`.
- Calls: a variadic seat `fn f(a, ..rest: List<T>)` with `f(a, 2, ..xs)` (`Param.variadic`, `DeclFacts.variadic`; extras expand into seats in `Checks.placed`, packed with the one list-building verb `listed`); `f(..opts)` filling named seats from a record's fields (`SeatFill`, shared by typing and lowering; the operand runs once); a spread field pins a type parameter as a written argument does (`FieldPin`, unified in `generic_call`). body:
`std-ui` `tests/loop_adversarial` failed under `AVRA_SCHED_SEED=4` on main's own tree: `zero wait: text "n=1 m=0"` where the golden said `n=0 m=0` (witnessed by ui-crash and reproduced here: `eval != expected under schedule 4`; seeds 1 and 3 pass).

**The law.** `later(ms(0))` promises that its act is eligible at once. It promises nothing about the screen read right after the ask: the loop and the test body are tasks, and under a seeded schedule any runtime call (the channel post inside `later` itself) is a scheduling point. The test asserted an ordering the scheduler does not promise, so the test is changed, not the loop.

**Not a code fix.** A first attempt made `advance(ms(0))` yield nothing; seed 4 still failed, because the ask's own post can run the job. It was reverted.

- The test reads the screen after `advance(ms(1))`, where the zero wait has run under every schedule; the golden line is `zero wait, once a millisecond has gone: text "n=1 m=0"`.
- `Screen.advance`'s doc said "a zero wait drains nothing a job still has to start", which is false under a seeded schedule. It now states what is promised (the span has gone by and the timers due in it have fired) and what follows the schedule (whether the turn they leave has run when it returns).

Proof: the fixed test under `AVRA_SCHED_SEED` 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 — all eight give `eval == native == expected`.

Whether a test harness should own the loop so the screen is deterministic by construction is a separate design question, sent to the lead.

body:
The flake filed as avra-8sb5.59.44.13 is a HANG on end of input, not a race between a key and the close.

**The bug.** A terminal app reads stdin as park, then read, then park again. When the peer has already written and closed before the app first parks, the first wake carries the data and the close together. The read drains the bytes; the close stays behind it as a sticky `READ_CLOSED` flag, and the poller reports an edge only once. The second park filed a waiter, found the flag set, and waited for an edge that never came: the app never saw the end of its input.

**The fix.** `waits_fd` claims a read waiter at once when the descriptor's peer has finished. One line in `runtime/avra_fiber.c`.

**Evidence.**
- Reproduced by hand on Linux: `printf abc | app` hung 20 of 20 times (exit 124 under `timeout`); with the writer slow (`(sleep 1; printf abc) | app`) or an empty pipe it ended. strace showed `epoll_wait` returning `EPOLLIN|EPOLLHUP` once, a read of 3 bytes, then a wait forever.
- Failing first: `runtime/tests/fiber_test.c` gains a reader that parks and reads until it finds the end, over a pipe written and closed before any reader ran. Without the fix `fiber_test` hangs; with it, 27 checks, 0 failed. The other runtime tests (adversarial, flow, tasks_door, clock, cores, seed) pass.
- Stress on the Sprite with the fix: the failing input `a\377b\t\n` fed to the terminal test app 200 times serially and 4 x 50 in parallel, all giving `name=[ab] hits=1`; 0 bad.

**Also.** The terminal's reader now posts with `post_unowned`: a key belongs to the app, never to whichever control a turn happens to be running for. This is construction, not the cause of the flake; I could not make a test fail without it, so none is added.

body:
## Cause
The order's front `(landing)` could be a PR that could not merge. Logs: `#892/#887/#871 waits behind #866 (landing)` for 19:18 to 20:12Z passes, while `#866 still BLOCKED on the required test check (not run yet)`; at 20:46 `#866 waits behind #893 (landing)`. Two paths reached it:
1. `_landing` read the lazy `mergeStateStatus` field for a green PR, so green + behind + field CLEAN counted as landing (and #874 patched only the input in `collect`; the decision still keyed on the field and the refresh dedup key `refresh:N:head` never retried a refresh that moved nothing).
2. Refresh asks were deduped per head only: an ask that did not move the head (or `main` moved again) was never repeated ("refresh asked").

I could not reproduce the 70 min stall from a single log line; the live dry run shows the remaining legitimate case: #893 is BEHIND but its own checks are still running, so it is landing by the lead's rule (b).

## Fix (tools/pr_watcher.py)
- `_lacks_main(p)`: exact `behind_by` from the compare, or an explicit BEHIND; the field can only add BEHIND, never clear it.
- `_landing`: armed AND (running its own checks OR green AND not lacking main). Green+behind is never landing, so it becomes the front and is refreshed.
- Refresh dedup key now `refresh:N:head:<main sha>`, so an ask that moved nothing is retried once main moves.
- `collect` records `behind_by` on each green PR.
- (a) Rule (n): newest of main's last 5 commits touching `.github/ci/` with no `ci-image` run on it or later gets `gh workflow run ci-image.yml --ref main`, once per commit (marked in state, and the run list is the second dedup since the state cache save is denied).

## Fixtures (`--self-test`, 32 plan scenarios + cases, passing)
- green+behind front is refreshed even when the API says CLEAN (`behind_by=1`), and the PR behind it is not told it waits on a "landing" PR
- `_landing` table: running, green+up-to-date, green+behind (count and field), unarmed, never-ran
- ci-image dispatched for an uncovered `.github/ci` merge, not when covered, not twice
- refresh retried only when main moved

## Live dry run (`python3 tools/pr_watcher.py --dry-run`, 2026-10-17)
```
pr-watcher: note 892 #892 waits behind #893 (landing)
pr-watcher: #893  BEHIND ... -> comment    (armed, own checks still running: landing by rule b)
pr-watcher: #866  BLOCKED ... -> comment
pr-watcher: dry run — no queue: 0 arm(s), 0 refresh(es), 0 cancel(s)
```
No `ci-image` dispatch owed right now (no recent `.github/ci` merge uncovered).

## Cause (by measurement)
Repro on main d76ec8f8: `avra test packages/std-ui/src/tests/instance_page` cold passes; append `// x` to `packages/std-ui/src/web/web.av`, re-run warm: `Basic Block in function 'av_avra_ui_event' does not have terminator!`.

Probing `emit_mode` (QTRACE) showed `l.fns` holding TWO bodies named `avra_ui_event` in the failing module: the real one (41 ins) and a held stub (0 ins). A host fn is a root, so it lowers even where its file is held; `Workspace.homed` (compiler/build.av) then stood `held_stubs(self)` beside `stay`, which already held the real body. `emit_mode` selects bodies to emit by NAME (`mine`), so the empty stub was emitted too: an `entry` block with no terminator. Cold builds have no held stubs, hence no duplicate. The failing derivation is the 3-attempt one (`Q attempt 1 hold true homes true reading 26`: instantiations owed from held homes).

Also: `wreck()` wrote the failed module's text at the store's `.o` path, so the next run served that text as the object (the "kept bad object" in the repro).

## Fix
- `homed`: `undeclared(held_stubs(self).concat(owed), lo.fns)` — a stub stands only where nothing lowered the symbol.
- `wreck`: writes `<path>.wreck`, never the object path; a failed verification never leaves an object in the store.

## Witness
`tools/host_fn_edit_attack.sh` (in `cache-attacks-b2`): edits `@std/ui`'s host-fn file three ways (comment line, body line, local renamed), builds each WARM and requires a pass, and requires that no store `.o` holds module text. Before the fix: 3/3 FAIL with the terminator error. After: 0 failed. The two extra shapes (body edit, local rename) are the red-team ones.

Not run: full `make cache-attacks`/gate (a fixture-only repro did not trigger it: the trigger needs owed instantiations from held homes, which `instance_page` provides).

Ticket avra-8sb5.59.44.9. Stacked on #887 (`ui-tui-width`).

A layout solver (`place`) that is CSS flexbox over the `Layout` vocabulary, and the web target made to write the whole vocabulary, so one view lays out alike on a page and in a terminal. A Firefox differential (`tools/layout-oracle`) runs random trees through the REAL html realizer and through the solver and demands every box agree.

## What a page will see (each is a behaviour change)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **Box model** | content-box: `width:8px` plus padding came out wider than 8 | `*{box-sizing:border-box}`: a fixed size is its own number; a box is never narrower than its padding |
| **`Fixed(n)`** | `width:Npx` only; the default `flex-shrink:1` squeezed it when a sibling asked for room (probe: row 60, pad 4+4, gap 1, `[Fixed 10, Fill]` gave the Fixed child **8.23**) | `.dir-row>.w-N{flex-shrink:0}` / `.dir-col>.h-N{flex-shrink:0}`: it holds its size on its parent's main axis |
| **`Fill`** | `width:100%`: beside a sibling or a gap it overflows, or shrinks the siblings (same probe: Fill 42.77 where 41 was meant) | takes the room that is left: on the parent's main axis `flex:var(--grow) 1 0%;min-width:0` (a `grow` given is its share; the 0% basis is the content's when the parent's size is not yet known), across it `align-self:stretch` |
| **`wrap`** | ignored by the web | `wrap-no` / `wrap-yes` / `wrap-rev` (`flex-wrap`) |
| **`margin`** | ignored by the web | `margin-inline-start/-end`, `margin-top/-bottom` per token |
| **`order`** | ignored by the web | `order-N` (negative as `order-nN`) |
| **`grow`** | `flex-grow:N` | `flex-grow:N;--grow:N`, with `--grow` an `@property` that does NOT inherit (a plain custom property leaked a parent's grow into a Fill child; the oracle found it) |
| **A row of unbreakable items on a terminal** | wrapped onto a new line | overflows exactly as a page does (rows no longer wrap by default); the tui adopts this in rung B with a golden change |

Short content in a `Fixed` box used to let the box shrink on the web; it no longer does.

`aspect` and `inset` are read by neither; `Percent` reads as `Hug` until the language converts a float to an int (avra-8sb5.10.177).

## The solver

- `place(tree, Measure, width) -> Placed`; `Measure` is the one place a unit lives (`own`, `kept`, `min_own`, `gap_x/gap_y`, `pad_x/pad_y`). `Cells` answers in terminal cells from the tui's own leaf shapes.
- Faithful flexbox: flex base size = max-content, automatic minimum = min-content, the freeze-and-clamp loop for grow AND shrink, fit-content cross sizes, line stretch, wrap-reverse mirroring, unsafe centring on overflow, definite/indefinite container sizes.
- Lengths travel in sixtieths of a unit (a browser's own LayoutUnit); boxes are handed back snapped by absolute edge, halves up.
- Sizes memoized per node and width (64000 rows place in 0.4 s native).

## The oracle

`node tools/layout-oracle/oracle.mjs --cases N --seed S`: each tree is rendered by `realize.html.html.render` and loaded in Firefox, and placed by `place` with a pixel measure over the theme's spacing. Failing trees are shrunk and printed with both answers. Your probe tree is fixed case 0. Seeds 1, 2, 4: 151 of 151 trees agree.

Measured (probe runs 39034809317, 39035774357): the serial IR->LLVM build of a cold std-avrac scoped run is 28-51 s over ~1,160 modules, flat 18-49 ms per module whatever its size, and ~75% of it is `emit_mode` scanning ALL 28,616 bodies about five times per module (own filter, hosted map, `declare_user` over every body, the bodies loop, plus a static scan): own-scan 10.0 s + scans/declares 11.5 s + bodies 6.4 s + declare_runtime 0.4 s of 28.3 s.

`emit_index(l)` builds, once per `handed()`/`program_objects()` call, position maps (name -> positions in `l.fns`, file -> positions, homeless positions, bucket cache per `of`, hosted names, static positions). A module visits the positions it owns / names / reads, sorted, so it sees exactly the sequence the scans visited, in the same order, duplicates included, and writes the same bytes. `Owned.defined_at` replaces `defines`/`owns` (now unused, removed); `refs_of`, `in_read_order`, `emit_object`, `emit_closed` take the index.

**What it does**

body:
`unsupported_on_wasm` (compiler/backend/llvm.av) scanned every lowered body, but a build lowers WHOLE FILES (objects are cached per file), so a program was refused for a row named only by a body nothing reaches: `use @std.time.{ms}` alone (std-time's sleeping verbs), or an uncalled `fn nap() { avra_fiber_sleep(1) }` with no import at all.

## The change
The refusal reads `Program.reached()` = `lowered()` (the program lowered FROM ITS ENTRY) instead of the build's whole-file lowering. No new walk: lowering's own `union`/`drained` already decides what an entry reaches. `reached()` is a QUERY: `lowered_bodies` takes a `settle` flag and the query passes false, so the scheduler bit (`record_schedulers`) stands as the build settled it and nothing is written then restored (an earlier draft restored it; that was a side effect wearing a query's name). Only wasm builds call it. `@std/time` names `wasm_objects` (its one C fn is a portable clock read), so the package-C half stops refusing; `wasm-refuses` still refuses `@std/process`.

## Why not reuse something else (the three candidates, quoted)
1. **lowering's `union`** (compiler/lower/lower.av:437): `bodies = if entry == null || every { flatten([declared(a) for a in files]) } else { [self.plain_want(d) for d in hosted] }`, then `drained(wants…)`. With an entry and `every == false` this IS a reach, and it is what this PR reuses. The BUILD does not ask for it: derive.av `bodies_lowered` calls `p.files_checked()` = `lowered_as(null, true, true)` (entry null, every, programs) so that each file's object holds every declared body. So `d.lowered.fns` is every declared body, not a reach.
2. **#705's links bit** (`Program.lowered_bodies`, `members_link_scheduler`, `root_links`): decides whether ANY member or the entry root links a scheduler: `unheld_decls().any(member && call_links)`, plus the entry file's own waits. It answers a yes/no over all members, not which bodies the entry reaches.
3. **CancelReach family** (compiler/cancel_reach.av, `parks`/`spins`/`links`): a per-fn "may reach a cancel point / a scheduler" bit, spread from every member with evidence to its CALLERS ("linear in the call graph"). It runs in the opposite direction (callee evidence to callers) and over all members, so it cannot say "is this body reached from the entry".

An earlier draft of this PR wrote a separate walk over `refs_of`; replaced by the reuse above (one definition of reach).

## Trigger
Reach belongs to the DB as a query eventually (what an entry reaches, kept as a relation, so the build, the cancel pass and this check ask one answer). Recorded as a trigger, not a move now.

## Cost (wasm build of the board, Sprite, wall seconds)

Fixes P0 avra-8sb5.57.271: the compiler TRAPPED (`index 129 is out of bounds (length 124)`) depending on what an earlier run left in the store. Seen as the second scoped `avra test` in one job, in CI's seed recovery, and as the "index 129" every DB lane hit.

## DB 09 precursor — the whole-row read is retired

`reads_rows_whole` returned `true` for `LiftLowered`, `Lifted` and `Settled` — the last three.
A compile-time run read a declaration's row and recorded the file's whole `Items` edge, so an
edit to any declaration in any file the run touched moved the run.

### What became per-declaration
- **`wire_siblings`** records the **NAME's bucket**, never the file's `Items`. The wire index is
  built from rows read unrecorded (`wire_rows`), so the one edge a reader owes is the only one left.
- **`Lifted` is a NAMED answer**: its `LiftAsk` keeps the call's expression, so its name spells the
  crossed annotation and the call's place inside it — durable wherever the file sits. Registered
  beside `named_units`. (`Settled`/`LiftLowered` were already named on main.)
- **The kernel whole-family grain is deleted**: `whole_families`/`reads_whole`/`reading_whole` and
  `Asker.whole` are gone; `row_read` always records the name's bucket. No family reads rows whole.

_Scope note: this retires the kernel grain; the cross-process verdict was already fine-grained in
`kept_settle.av`. The observable win is the in-process edit path, not the stood/ran verdict._

body:
A design note from the channels campaign's perf review, prompted by the owner's questions: **can refcounting have non-refcounting speed**, and what is the **copy-on-read** cost.

It separates three overheads that are usually conflated — **(a) counts, (b) headers, (c) indirection** — and says plainly that RC elision fixes only (a): a stream of boxed records pays the header and the indirection however perfect the counts are.

- **Part 1**: RC semantics, ownership-typed codegen — Perceus (Koka, PLDI 2021): borrow inference (Avra has it), dup/drop specialisation and reuse (Avra does not), so ownership is INFERRED and counts are emitted only where sharing is unavoidable. Names what Avra already has and what is missing (incl. cycles — the 922 MB weak-capture leak).
- **Part 2**: representation — the element type decides the layout (slab / flat struct array / handle / ring), with an escape hatch; P12 applied to memory.
- **Part 3**: where the passes live (an `Ownership` facts table consumed by the memory pass; a cell read-modify-write pass) and on iterating to a fixpoint — cheap here because passes are memoized queries, bounded and priced like everything else.
- **Part 4**: the census (all three counts) decides the ORDER of the fixes, not the choice.

Docs only — no compiler, runtime or package change.
title: docs: memory, ownership and representation — RC with non-RC speed

`dial_ready` read the scheduler's descriptor bit, armed optimistically the
moment a `select` filed the dial's wake — so a socket still connecting read
as ready. It now settles from the kernel alone: `getpeername` answers the
peer once the connection stands, `SO_ERROR` names the refusal once it has
failed, and a connect that has answered neither is not ready. The `armed`
cell retires; `dial_wait` holds the same law for the blocking `next`.

`packages/std-net/src/tests/race_ready` proves both halves on loopback — the
race answers the first dial that connects, and a connect whose listener's
backlog is full (its SYN is dropped, so it stays in progress) answers the
race's own deadline, never a descriptor. `eval == native == expected`; the
test fails against the optimistic-bit dial.

Base: rung 1 (`origin/flow-06-runtime`, PR #771) — the row, its C body, the `W_SIG` waiter and the **seed refresh that carries the row** — merged into `origin/flow-06-sources` (PR #770, `Source.arm`), whose seed conflict resolved to rung 1's seed (the one carrying the row).

## The row is ARMED

| | |
|---|---|
| host | `RtHost.Unhosted` → `RtHost.WaitSig` (`core/runtime_api.av`) |
| evaluator arm | `wait_sig_val` (`compiler/backend/interp_tasks.av`), calling `avra_vtask_wait_sig` on the interpreter's own virtual task |
| dispatch | `.WaitSig` in `compiler/backend/interp.av` |
| native | unchanged — `llvm_emit`'s `settled_valued` reaches `rest ->` and the C body is called by name |
| new `Ins` / `boxes` | none — the seats stay words `(sig, arm, member)` |

## The declaration

`@std/task` declares `extern fn avra_wait_sig(sig: int, arm: int, member: int)` and lands the library spelling:

```avra
use @std.task.{signals, Sig, Source}
let quit: Source<Sig> = signals([.Int, .Term])
```

`Sig` is a closed set (`Hup Int Quit Term Usr1 Usr2 Pipe Alrm Chld`), each mapped to its number. **Members are per-signal**: `signals` files one wait per signal, `avra_wait_sig(number(s), arm, i)`, so several are waited on together and no aggregate crosses the row's word seats. `next` parks and reads the member the claim names.

## Proof

- **`packages/std-task/src/tests/signals`** — `signals([.Int, .Term])` parks a task, a spawned `sh -c 'kill -TERM $PPID'` signals the program, the wait answers `.Term` (member 1, the right one). **eval == native == expected == `term`.** The evaluator DOES carry a signal wait: `avra_vtask_wait_sig` files it on the same runtime policy, so `avra run` parks and wakes exactly as a compiled fiber.

- `./avra test packages/std-avrac` — 8907/8907 tests, 356 programs.
- `make seed-check` — **the seed compiles HEAD**. No re-seed: rung 1's seed carries the row; `RtHost.WaitSig` is read from source, and the seed never writes enum slots positionally.

## The defect

A `then` case's failure report (`show_case_failure` -> `show_diff`/`text_of_node`) read its compared operands through `cx.reg_of` AFTER `lower_fn` closed the case body's block scope. The memory pass releases the operands at that scope's exit, so the failure arm read a dropped register — a use-after-free in the pass's own output, proven by the L2 soundness check:

    error[language.defect]: in `tests.errors_adversarial_test$case217`, instruction 32 reads r14 after it was released

## The fix

The body's block scope stays OPEN across the report (`LowerCx.lower_block_open` / `lower_block_close`, `compiler/lower/walk.av`), used by `lower_fn` for a `.Case` body, so the failure arm is emitted INSIDE the frame that owns the operands and the scope-exit release lands after the read. `lower_block` is now the one-shot form of the same pair. No memory-pass rule changed: the read stays inside its defining span, which is what the pass's scope-based ownership assumes.

## Witness (Sprite `avra-triage`)

    14/14 tests passed

**CHANNELS campaign, FLOW 05 slice S0.** The foundational carrier the rest of FLOW 05 builds on. Draft: it exists to run `full-ci` and to carry the review; do not merge.

## What lands

`packages/std-task/` — `Source<T>`, `Sink<T>`, `TrySource<T, E>`, `AnyOf<T>`, `Channel<T>` and their verbs (`send`/`post`/`offer`/`close`; `ready`/`next`/`taken`/`ended`/`lost`), over FLOW 01/04's existing gate rows (`avra_gate_new`, `avra_wait_gate`, `avra_gate_claim`, `avra_wait_park`). **No new `rt_sigs` row and no new IR** — a channel is data + behaviour the waiting rows already state. Buffer, handed and pending counts live in Avra; a cancel decodes as `claim < 0` (arm minus one under this channel's arm 0).

A full send parks its sender on the givers gate; a reader claims one and moves its value into `handed`; a parked sender claimed for room retries into the buffer; a cancel claims a parked sender and the send answers `false` (the send-to-a-departed-reader cancel point).

## Proof

- `avra test packages/std-task`: 9/9, `channel_park: eval == native == expected`. A five-item producer through a channel of two never exceeds its bound.
- `runtime/tests/channel_gate_test.c`: 11 checks, `make runtime-tests` green, `make runtime-mutations` 350/350 killed.
- `avra fmt --check` and `avra check --baseline tools/idioms.baseline` clean.

## Forced choices (S1/S2 pending)

- `channel<T>(n)` cannot be named yet: `channel` is reserved (`resolve.reserved`), dropped in S1. S0 names the constructor `open_channel<T>(n)`; `unbounded_channel<T>()` is already free.
- A `Task` may not ride a record field or a fn answer until S2 (`type.task_escape`), so `Source`/`Sink` carry no `work: Task<bool>?` field, `ended` answers `bool` (not a task), and `offer` answers `Posted` (not `Offer`).
- `AnyOf` is non-parking (`ready`/`taken`) until S3's `select` needs `arm`/`take(member)`.
- Probe: a pinned generic call (`chan<int>(4)`) parses and types clean; `channel<int>(4)` refuses only on the reserved word.

DRAFT — do not merge (freeze: CHANNELS #710). Off `main` b0d98c49.

## The hole

`parse_grammar` answers a NON-NULL `built` whenever the start rule hits, plus a
`Cause.Trailing` diagnostic when tokens are left over. `build_grammar_lit`
tested only `if gp.built == null`, so a partial DSL parse became a tree
silently: every rule after the construct the seed could not read was dropped
with no refusal.

This is exactly how the `@operators` bring-up failed: a compiler whose DSL
predates `@operators` parsed `expr_spine`'s `grammar { ... }` up to the
`operators` rule and lost every rule after `stmt`, then reported
`expression: references undefined rule operators` — pointing nowhere near the
truncation.

## The fix

Refuse when `built` is absent OR any diagnostic is not a coherence defect
(`Cause.Defect`, no source anchor) — those are gated where the assembled
grammar validates, so this does not double-report them.

## Witness

New fixture: `grammar { a = "x" -> f() / b = }` — `rule+` matches `a`, stops
at `b =`, and the parse still answers a Grammar.

- With the refusal: `13/13 tests passed`.
- Refusal removed (one generation rebuilt on Sprite `avra-measure-ref`):
  `12/13 tests passed`, the failure naming exactly the new case
  (`grammar_lit_test.av:190`).

body:
**DRAFT — for review.**

## The measurement owed (20 runs, directory-suite convention)

`./avra test packages/std-avrac/src/features/tasks` 20 times on the main-based tree (`b0d98c49`, carries #691/#702/#706), cold eval each run, on the Sprite:

**20/20 green**, ~200 s per run, `32 programs proved` each. The `wait_set: eval != expected` flake does **not** reproduce on this base in clean sequential directory-suite runs. The moving field the notes named (`3:7` vs `2:9`) was never seen in these runs.

## A real defect in the same mechanism, found while measuring

The wait-set arm `avra_wait_fd(fd, writable, ...)` asks whether a descriptor is ready **now**, but the runtime's watch is edge-triggered (`EV_CLEAR`/`EPOLLET`, registered once). A direction that stayed ready since the wait that consumed the edge reports no new edge, so the next arm **parks** and its far deadline claims instead.

Witness: a program arming the same writable descriptor twice.

| leg | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `avra test .../writable_fd_twice` | `eval != expected` (`2:9 2:9`) | `eval == native == expected` (`3:7 3:7`) |
| eval (`avra run`) | `3:7 2:9` | `3:7 3:7` |
| native | `3:7 2:9` | `3:7 3:7` |
| `runtime/tests/flow_test.c` | `flow: 277 checks, 1 failed` (kqueue **and** epoll) | 0 failed |

The suite's `2:9 2:9` is the honest face of the fixture: the first eval disagrees, the held derivation is discarded, and the fresh re-evaluation's *first* arm already finds the edge consumed. This is also why `wait_set` — which arms once per process — can only flake once something forces that re-evaluation.

## The fix

`fd_refresh` re-adds the watched direction (`EV_ADD|EV_CLEAR` on kqueue, `EPOLL_CTL_MOD` on epoll) before the poller is asked, so the level it holds now is the answer. It runs **only for a level wait** (`avra_wait_fd` / `avra_vtask_wait_fd`); `avra_fiber_park_fd`'s legacy edge park is byte-identical — its callers retry the read or write that found nothing.

## Checks (Sprite = Linux/epoll, Mac = kqueue)

- `make runtime-tests` 0 failed on both; the new check is in `flow_test`.
- `avra test packages/std-avrac/src/features/tasks` -> `33 programs proved`, status 0.
- `avra test packages/std-net` -> `15 programs proved`, status 0 (fd-park path unchanged).
- `avra fmt --check` on the new `.av`: 0 differing; `avra check packages/std-avrac --baseline tools/idioms.baseline`: 0.

Commits: witness first (`fdd59c52`), fix second (`eb7388fb`). No language surface change.

`start_recursive` answers a `.Cycle` by starting a new compute, so `Workspace.expanded(file)` re-ran its whole body once per re-entrant asker. #700 made the repeats statement-free; this removes the repeats themselves. A file's first re-entrant expansion while its run is open expands again and keeps what it settled in `Decls` for the run; a later re-entry in that run reads it. The outer run's end clears it, so a later revision starts with none.

Design note: the first attempt (`start_reentrant_once`, cycle path only in std-relation) left the previous revision's value Present in `values`, which a warm revision could read as stale. This keeps the state in `Decls`, keyed by file, created and retired by the expansion run itself — revision-scoped by construction.

Measured, cold `check packages/std-avrac` on #716 + #700, QTRACE `settle Expanded` per file: **173 settles for core/nodes.av → max 3 per file**; wall **132 s → 109 s**, peak unchanged (1859 MB), 0 errors.

body:
## What it is
A deadline is a cancel point at every wait, and the scope that asked is where it lands.

- `within d { body }` answers `Ok(body)` or `Err(TimedOut { after, at })`: the span it was
  given and the frames its unwind left. `match`, `?`, `catch` and a binding all hold it.
- A passed deadline UNWINDS a sleep, a join, a wait set's park, a descriptor park and a
  checked back-edge, in both engines. Before, only the back-edge did; a sleep and a join
  ran on, and a socket wait answered its verb's own timed-out error.
- Only the scope that asked answers. An inner `within … catch` under an outer deadline is
  passed untouched; a task under an INHERITED limit unwinds to its top and ends cancelled
  by the scope's id.
- A block that answers nothing is refused by name (`type.within`); so is a `within` in a
  program that loads no `@std/time` (a lone source). `TimedOut` stays `@std/time`'s.

## How it is built
- Runtime (`runtime/avra_fiber.c`): `avra_fiber_within_end` is the LANDING — 1, and the
  unwind bit cleared, only when the scope's own request stood and the task was unwinding.
  One predicate (`claimed_by_cut`) and one pre-park check (`deadline_stands`) serve every
  wait; the evaluator's twins agree (`avra_vtask_cut`, `avra_vtask_join_parked`).
- Compiler: `features/tasks/check.av` types it, `lower.av`'s epilogue answers
  landed -> `Err`, still unwinding -> pass on, else `Ok`. Every body's cold exit pushes its
  static frame (`avra_unwind_push`, a `Pure` row so a compile-time run still settles).
- No new rt_sigs row, no core/ir.av change.

## The order inside this PR (why the seed moves)
The compiler links `@std/http`, whose SOURCE spelled `within` 15 times, so the flip is a
change the compiler checks about its own source:
1. the flip — a pre-flip compiler builds gen-1;
2. std-http's source sites — gen-1 builds gen-2, the fixed point;
3. `make seed` from that fixed point — bootstrap and seed-check pass again.
CI's cached main compiler cannot read this tree and falls to the committed seed, as designed.

## The preserve rule
Every existing site keeps what it answered. A `within` over a fallible verb is wrapped by
the helper of its error currency, and nothing else on the line or in its arms changes:

| | home | folds `Err(TimedOut)` into |
|---|---|---|
| H0 `outran` | std-net/src/net.av | (the mint) a `NetError`, `timed_out()` true |
| H1 `timely` | std-net/src/net.av | `NetError` |
| H2 `tls_timely` | std-tls/src/tls.av | `TlsError.Net` |
| H3 `wire_timely` | std-http/src/wire.av | `WireError.Net` |
| H4 `in_stage` | std-http/src/client.av | `ClientError.TimedOut(stage)` |
| H5 `or_quiet` | std-io/src/watch/watch.av | `.Ok(.Quiet)` |

Blocks that cannot time out unwrap (`catch _ -> 0`). Two sites could not be preserved:
- `std-http/src/quota.av:133` — a handler past its bound is unwound, so a status is chosen:
  `408 "the body did not arrive in time"` (what today's failed body read was worded as).
- `std-http/src/tests/pool_wait_test.av:111` — a take under the task's shorter `within`
  is cut, where it answered `Exhausted`; the case asserts the cut and no second dial.

## Proof
Measured on a Sprite at the head under the seed commit, then again after it:
- fixed point: `make avra` twice, same binary; `make bootstrap` ("the seed IS this tree") and `make seed-check` green on the committed seed.
- `make runtime-tests` green (flow 286 checks, vtasks 61); `make runtime-mutations` 303 of 303 killed.
- keepers: externs, flow-trace, witnesses, fmt-lossless, ui-board, rt-header, rt-ns, vocab, codecs, fingerprints.
- suites: features/tasks 45/45 + 36 programs · defers 104/104 + 6 · results 85/85 + 7 · core 290/290 + 2 · std-time 23/23 + 10 · std-net 94/94 + 15 · std-io 115/115 + 2 · std-tls 64/64 + 5 · std-https 19/19 + 7 · std-http 1330/1330 + 35 · std-process 119/119 + 3.
- seen flaking, not this PR's: std-net `tests/unwound` (a resolver thread's wake end against a 200 ms wait) — 3 of 9 in-suite runs on the Sprite, green in the final pass.

## What is owed
- `TimedOut` and `Cancelled` to `@std/prelude` — a follow-up that moves the real types
  (`Duration`, `Frame`/`Loc` are in the way); no twin record here.
- A `within` over a block answering nothing stays refused — ticketed.
- `defer within d { … }` as one phrase (avra-8sb5.10.172); one generic fold for the four
  `*_timely` helpers (ROADMAP interim record).
- Under a deadline's own unwind, a `defer`'s wait is cut at once even inside the defer's
  `within` (a scope opened under a standing request never asks).
- The evaluator's yield arm does not meet a cancel that already stands.

Stacked on #618. DB 06 step 4 (avra-8sb5.57.175, .203).

A `@query` answer is kept with the reads it stood on, and read back only while every digest stands (law L3).
- A relation read is flattened to `(relation name, hash of its rows)`. The hash is the relation's own maintained set hash: O(1), nothing recomputed per restore, no per-revision memo needed. A write to another relation moves nothing.
- An input read is `(input name, spelled arguments, value hash)`; a query read stands for what that query stood on.
- A read of rows no open query hears (another Db's) makes the answer unsaved.
- Retired: `rows_alone`, `Db.restored`, `Db.writes`, `read_restored`, `restored_cell`, `unsettles_restored`.
- The flattening is a named, bounded imprecision, retired by DB 07a (design doc §5.3).

Proof (Sprite): `std-relation` 243/243, 6 refusals proved, durable program eval == native == expected. durable.av now pins: .203's two cases turned right (`12 01`), an unrelated relation's write moves nothing in this process or the next, a write to the read relation does, an input moved between processes is a miss and set back is a hit, an unrelated input set moves nothing (`fixed fixed 0`). With the digest comparison and the foreign-read taint removed, durable goes red.

Cost: relation digest O(1); `check packages/cli` unchanged 204-216 ms with this compiler (the compiler's own checks never reach the restore path). Not measured: restore of a compiler-side query over `Decl` — none exists on the warm check path.

Known gaps: a lazily loaded `@input` not yet asked in the new process is a miss (conservative). Two inputs of one name and signature in different modules make a restore a miss (ambiguous name), never a hit.

Measured restore (Sprite, evaluator via `avra run`, ns timer): a `@query` answering `Dec.all(db).length`, 5000 rows, kernel already made — computed 11.3 ms; restored 1.3-1.9 ms; 50 rows: restored 0.9 ms. The restore is a fixed cost (name lookups, one O(1) hash compare, decode), not a function of the rows; under 5 ms.

Stacked on #527 (flow-12c); its commits show here until it lands.

## What it does
- **A bare `t.await` of a task that ended cancelled no longer traps.** The awaiter is cancelled by the same asker: `avra_task_join` installs the request on the caller (`cancel_passed`, through the one cancel door `fiber_cancelled`) and meets it at once (`cancel_met`, so the unwind's frame list begins empty). Its `defer`s run, and whoever joins IT is passed the same cancel in turn. A request that already stands is not displaced; a caller already unwinding takes on no other; a scope's end joining what it owns (`deaf`) passes nothing; under a shield the join keeps its trap.
- **Same in the evaluator** (`task_join_val` -> `cancel_passed`, over one new C door `avra_vtask_passed`). A run task that ends unwinding is now recorded cancelled with its asker (`finished`, over `avra_vtask_asker`) — it was recorded as answered by itself.
- **A cancelled `main` reports and exits 1**: `avra: main was cancelled — awaiting a task cancelled by task <id>` (`by main` for the run itself, ``by a `within` limit`` for a scope). ONE definition of the words, in C (`avra_main_cancelled_words`), read by both engines. Native: the emitted `main` answers `avra_main_ended(code)`, declared by the backend as `avra_args_init` is — no `rt_sigs` row, and it lives in the core runtime object so a program that never spawns links no scheduler. Evaluator: `Ended.Cancelled(words)`, exit 1 through `ended_as`, never the trap path. It reports a PASSED cancel only, never the bare unwind bit. No `<site>`: nothing writes `TASK_SITE` yet, so the words name only the asker.
- **Harness**: a third marker, `<name>.verdict` — exit 1 with that text on stderr, both engines, as a child. One `ChildEnd` enum (marker, exit code) read by discovery, `is_program` and the cli's leg judge.

## Measured (Sprite, Linux, this tree's compiler)
- Before (flow-12c head): `avra run …/cancelled_join.av` -> `avra: a join takes a task that answers, and this one was cancelled`, exit 2.
- After: `avra run` of `std-time/src/tests/cancelled_join` -> `avra: main was cancelled — awaiting a task cancelled by main`, exit 1; of `main_cancelled` (three deep, a fourth task asks) -> `main's defer ran` then `… cancelled by task 4`, exit 1.
- `avra test packages/std-time`: `3 refusals proved`, `7/7 tests passed`, `2 programs proved` (native and eval leg of each child test).
- `avra test packages/std-avrac/src/features/tasks`: 24 programs proved, `passed_cancel: eval == native == expected`, status 0.
- `program_files_test.av` 14/14; `cli/src/commands/tests/test_scope_test.av` 11/11 (a `.verdict` passes in both engines; a run that traps under one fails naming `wanted a verdict (code 1)`).
- `make runtime-tests`: status 0. `make runtime-mutations`: `268 of 268 killed, 265 by a failing check and 3 by the bound` — 16 new, 2 rewritten.
- `make vocab`: clean. `make keepers-static` (Mac): clean.

## Unverified / owed
- wasm and reactor entries are untouched: a wasm `main` answers the entry's code as before; no wasm run was made.
- `<site>` in the report.
- Under a shield the join traps; the compiler emits no shield bracket yet, so that arm is reached only by the C tests.

A plain fn or method that lowered without speaking is kept per file in the store under the file's surface, and a check serves it as a held want (stub + kept asks + kept code facts) while the file's text moved. An edit of one body lowers that body.

## main is red; this is why

main's push run 38201399908 fails `cache-attacks` (job 114655794954), which fails the required `test` check and blocks every PR. The exact failures:

```
FAIL  avra cache  is not avra explain --why
FAIL  avra cache changed is not avra explain --why
FAIL  avra cache held is not avra explain --why
FAIL  avra cache why is not avra explain --why of the file
FAIL  avra cache dependents is not avra explain of the file
cache-attacks: 340 builds through one store, 116 under a hold, 5 failed
```

`#474` ("explain: --why lists the answers a change reaches, and the cache aliases go") deliberately deleted `packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av`, removed `cache` from `main.av`, and moved its tests to `explain_holds_test`. ## The measurement (cli, warm Sprite, `check packages/cli --time`)

One body edit of `packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av`:

- baseline `warm edit` 35.4-35.9 s (`warm unchanged` 331 ms), `held 492/498`
- `attempt 0, discarded 1`
- `discarded: 11908ms — ast 8745ms, sublang 1047ms, load 11908ms`

## The discarded turn and WHY

`AVRA_QTRACE=1` prints `Q attempt 0 ... reading 0` then `Q attempt 1 ... reading 389`.
The turn is `unruled` (`compiler/derive.av`): 385 reads are `lead_reads`' (#468's
const-verdict pre-reads) and 4 are `Unruled` — `cli/src/commands/{explain,repr,run,writes}.av`,
held files whose kept rule findings no longer stand. The 4 turn the attempt.

A body edit to `shared.av` moves a compile-time read token (`key_parts.runs`), so the
four siblings that read it hold a key with no `rules` row. That move is only knowable
AFTER `settle_holds`/`unruled` resolve the pending reads, which parse ~144 files
(`load`, ast ~8.7 s). The next attempt repeats the exact same resolution — so the
attempt is paid in full. The validation (`unruled`) REQUIRES the work it discards.

## Fixes eliminated (each measured)

1. **Move `read_held_asks`/`read_held_codes` before `program`** (the DB 00d AsksUnread
   cause for std-avrac): cli `warm edit` 35.4-35.9 s -> 36.8-39.0 s, `discarded` still 1.
   The cli turn is `unruled`, not an unread asks row. Reverted.
2. **Extend `lead_reads` to pre-read every held file whose compile-time read text moved**:
   cli `warm edit` 53.1 s, `held 465/498` — a regression, because forcing the readers to
   be read lowers their bodies; the discard's cost is `load`, not the four files. Reverted.

## Conclusion

No minimal "validation before derivation" exists for this turn. The fix is DB 07's
per-declaration keys, so a rule-finding row cannot move with a sibling body edit.
This PR records the finding in `docs/2026_10_06_COMPILER_DB.md` section 7.2 and lands
no code change (neither candidate moved the number; one regressed).

DRAFT — a finding, not a fix.

Two attempts. The first is discarded:

Parses split at the second `Q attempt`: **178 during the discarded attempt's `load`**, **181 after**.

The `load`-phase parses are `resolve_pending_reads` in `derive.av` (it parses each pending run-read to compare the referenced declaration's syntax). Traced: `Q pending` fires 104 times, **all on `shared.av`**, from 14 readers — so that path parses ONE file and is not the 178.

The DB 07 acceptance (avra-8sb5.57.176) is a warm `check packages/cli`.
The **goal** is <= 60 ms unchanged and <= 300 ms after one body edit
(goal 150). #552 landed the bench but it SKIPPED when no warm store stood
and no row keyed the runner, so CI was green while the path was hundreds of
times over.

**How the store reaches CI.** `prepare` already hands `.avra-cache` down
inside `avra-build.tar` (the same hand-down the gate and suites read);
`keepers-a` untars it. A `warm the store` step in `prepare` guarantees one
stands even on an exact-key release hit (empty store -> one
`check packages/cli` under the binary being handed down, so the store is
keyed to the keeper's compiler).

**What "skip" does now.** A run that cannot judge FAILS with a named
reason:
```
warm_edit_bench: no warm store at .avra-cache
warm_edit_bench: this is a FAILURE — the warm-edit gate cannot judge; ...
```
The ONLY skip is the `warm_skip` `workflow_dispatch` input ->
`WARM_EDIT_SKIP`, and it says so loudly. `speed_ratchet.py --warm` refuses
a skip stream the same way; `tools/witness_warm_edit.sh` proves both
directions.

## The ceilings are the STARTING LINE, not the goal

A ratchet's ceiling is seeded from the **measured present** and may only
fall. The goal stands as a **comment** in `tools/speed.budget`, never as
the enforced value: a row seeded at the goal refuses every run and nothing
can land — which is exactly how this PR was blocked (main measured
hundreds of times over 60/300).

Seeded from real runs, not aspirational targets:

| host | unchanged | edit | where it came from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-warm` | **314 ms** | **23216 ms** | the worse of two same-commit runner runs (the other was 194 ms / 14824 ms) |
| `linux-x86-64-amd-epyc` | **23789 ms** | **68208 ms** | the DB 07 lane's Sprite present on main |

**Tolerance: `WARM_RATIO = 2.0`.** The two runner runs of ONE commit spread
**1.62x** apart (194 <-> 314, 14824 <-> 23216) — the runner is shared and
the warm figure is load-sensitive. A ratchet that flakes is worse than
none: it teaches people to ignore it. So the gate allows 2x the seeded row;
a run must beat 2x the seeded present before it fires, which is a real
regression rather than ordinary variance. `--warm --accept` may only
**lower** a row (never raise), so the ceiling walks down toward the goal as
the profiling lanes fix the cost.

## Witnessed both directions

- **The seed is honest** — both observed runner runs PASS:
  `unchanged 194ms vs ceiling 314ms (limit 628ms)` and
  `unchanged 314ms vs ceiling 314ms (limit 628ms)` (edit likewise).
- **A regression FAILS by name:**
  ```
  speed: FAIL: warm unchanged: 700ms vs ceiling 314ms (limit 628ms), goal 60ms (over by 72ms)
  speed: FAIL: warm edit: 50000ms vs ceiling 23216ms (limit 46432ms), goal 150ms (over by 3568ms)
  ```
- **A skip still FAILS** (`speed: REFUSED — the warm-edit measurement was
  skipped (skip warm-edit), and a skip is not a pass`), and only
  `WARM_EDIT_SKIP` stands it down, loudly.
- `tools/witness_warm_edit.sh`, `speed_ratchet.py --self-test` (34
  fixtures), `ci_invariants.py --self-test` and `make keepers-static` all
  pass.

## Budget rows seeded

```
ci-warm warm edit 23216
ci-warm warm unchanged 314
linux-x86-64-amd-epyc warm edit 68208
linux-x86-64-amd-epyc warm unchanged 23789
```
Keyed by `SPEED_HOST=ci-warm` (not the runner's CPU). `--warm --accept`
may only lower one.

*Note: the `linux-x86-64-amd-epyc` pair is the lane's Sprite present as
reported on main; it is a store-mismatch/cold price, not the warm price,
and is owed a warm measurement on that host. The CI rows are the ones the
gate actually judges.*

body:
## Why nothing has been landing

`main` has not moved since 11:20 UTC. Every armed PR's required `test` is
red, and the failure is **not** the `suites` aggregate.

Read the real run of #531 (`38135212651`, the `test` job log):

```
test: PASSED
...
speed: FAIL: wall prepare: 987000ms vs ceiling 650000ms (over by 337000ms)
speed: FAIL: wall total: 4215562ms vs ceiling 1200000ms (over by 3015562ms)
speed: REFUSED — 2 wall row(s) past the ceiling or unjudged
```

The verdict printed `test: PASSED`; the **wall-budget step** refused. Every
`suites (...)` leg in that run was `success`. Where `test: FAILED — suites`
did appear (`flow-12c`, `db-03b-codec-growth`, `own-db-law`), the jobs API
shows a matrix leg genuinely **failed** (1 failure / 3 success) — GitHub's
aggregate is the correct worst-of-its-legs, so the four suspects in the
ticket (skipped counted as failed, wrong needs, cancelled leg, fail-fast)
are all ruled out: `fail-fast: false`, and `skipped` is already green.

The real cause is the collision of two landings:

- **#565** dropped the merge queue and made the PR itself the gate — every
  PR runs keepers, `seed-check` and the suites.
- **#568** added `tools/speed.budget`'s `ci-wall` ceilings, calibrated for
  the *fast floor* the PR used to be.

So a PR that builds its own compiler costs ~16 min of `prepare` and ~70 min
of summed job clock, and the 650 s / 1200 s ceilings refused **every**
full-gate PR from the hour they landed.

## The fix

1. **`tools/speed.budget`** — the `ci-wall` ceilings recalibrated to the
   full gate the completed runs measured: `prepare 1300 s`, `gate 650 s`,
   `total 7000 s`. The #531 metrics that died on the old rows now pass.
2. **`tools/ci_verdict.py`** (new, self-tested) — the `test` verdict reads
   the `test` job's own `needs:` as the expected set and the run's `needs`
   JSON as what happened. A skipped leg **by design** is green; any other
   result is refused by name **with the count**; a job the gate owed but
   the run never reported is refused too. `make ci-verdict` is a
   compiler-free keeper, so the fixtures run on every PR.
3. **`docs/2026_10_12_CI_BUDGET.md`** — corrected: `total` is the SUM of
   the job clocks, not the makespan, and the ceilings are the full gate's.

## Witnesses

The real #531 metrics now pass:

```
speed: PASS: wall gate: 498000ms vs ceiling 650000ms
speed: PASS: wall prepare: 987000ms vs ceiling 1300000ms
speed: PASS: wall total: 5182000ms vs ceiling 7000000ms
speed: clean — 3 wall row(s) within the ceiling
```

A job past its ceiling still refuses:

```
speed: FAIL: wall total: 7290000ms vs ceiling 7000000ms (over by 290000ms)
speed: REFUSED — 3 wall row(s) past the ceiling or unjudged
```

The verdict, on a genuinely failing leg (not just a green run):

```
test: FAILED — 1 of 11 not green (1 failure, 2 skipped, 8 success)
test:   suites: failure
```

and on the real passing set:

```
test: PASSED — 2 skipped, 9 success (11 needed)
```

`make ci-verdict`, `make ci-invariants`, `make keepers-static` and
`make pipeline-doc` all pass locally.
title: ci: unblock the PR gate — the wall budget is the full gate's, and the verdict names its arithmetic

The runtime half of flow-03 14b. Three word/ptr rows —
`avra_unwind_push(frame: ptr)`, `avra_unwind_count() -> int`,
`avra_unwind_at(i: int) -> ptr` — with the frame store, its cap and its
reset, and no compiler push yet.

- The store is per TASK, on the task record (not the pooled Fiber), so a
  joiner can read it after the task ended; the program's own run keeps
  its own (`g_main_unwind`).
- Cap 16: on the 17th push the middle (index 8) is dropped and counted;
  `avra_unwind_dropped()` answers the count the landing will fold into
  one `Frame`.
- Reset at the CANCEL POINT (`cancel_met`, the bit's 0-to-1 transition),
  not at a landing: a passed-through landing does not clear, and each
  unwind's list is exactly its own. `cancel_met` now sets the bit once.
- Rung 3: `runtime/avra_rt.h` and `features/rt.av` are regenerated from
  the rows (`make rt-header`/`rt-ns`), so the C bodies are held to the
  row shapes by `_Static_assert` and a `LowerCx` spells a typed call.
- The cap is pinned as a program test (`unwind_cap`) in both engines:
  sixteen kept, the middle dropped, the newest eight follow.
- The runtime tests gain `the_cap_drops_the_middle`,
  `the_programs_own_run_pushes` and `a_cancel_point_begins_the_list`; the
  mutation set gains the eight lines.

What is owed, and why:

- The COMPILER push (`LowerCx.frame`, the `static_read` plus push in
  `unwinds()`) lands with 14d, together: until 14d reads `at`, a push has
  no consumer. Nothing in this PR emits `avra_unwind_push`.
- The committed SEED refresh is the lead's. This branch does not
  `make seed`; the rows and their declaration land first, the seed after.
- An `unwind_reset` program test was dropped. The reset is real (proved
  in C), but Avra cannot observe it yet: a cancelled task unwinds past
  the bare park in BOTH engines (probed), and the only same-task view
  during the unwind is a `defer`, whose cancel leg diverges — native runs
  it, the evaluator does not — and that divergence is PRE-EXISTING on
  `origin/main` (probed with main's own compiler: eval `-1`, native `7`).
  The Avra-observable read is 14d's joiner. Owed with that.

Gate (this machine, load ~40-60, disk ~2 GB free):

- `make keepers-static` clean; `rt-header`, `rt-ns`, `witnesses`,
  `dogfooding-rules`, `footprint`, `attack` clean.
- `fmt --check` on the 7 changed `.av` clean; `check packages/std-avrac
  --baseline` clean.
- `make runtime-tests`: the new frame checks pass; 3 failures, all the
  known load flake (`the waiter has left by its time`, flow_test.c 1147/
  1150/1151), pre-existing and unrelated.
- `make runtime-mutations`: 229 of 229 killed, 0 survive.
- NOT run locally: the full `gate_changed --refs origin/main HEAD` (its
  ~38 affected packages write several GB of cache and the disk held
  ~2 GB); `speed-ratchet` and `warm-edit` refused on wall clock under
  load (build lower 13.0 s vs 2.5 s ceiling; warm edit 38.3 s vs 0.3 s).
  Let the PR's CI be the gate for those.

Groundwork for DB 07 (b/c): two over-invalidations on the one-edit hold path, each a whole-file read where a declaration read is true. **This does not yet move the DB 07 speed number** (see Measurements); what remains is stated below.

## What changes

- `recorded_reads`' `decl_for_body` matched only a declaration's own symbol, so a `const` initializer body — named by its settle symbol `settled_symbol(const_symbol(f, s), seats)` — fell through to a plain whole-file read: editing one body in that file moved every reader of the const. It now resolves to its const declaration, matching the base **exactly** (or the base + its `@<fps>` seat suffix), never by a bare prefix, since `const_symbol` ends in `const<index>` and a prefix would resolve index 12 to index 1 — an under-invalidation that holds the reader on the wrong declaration.
- `unruled` judged held files by `held_okey` after `settle_holds` had already resolved pending reads: a key asked here opened a fresh `?<print>` pending marker that nothing resolved, forcing read a reader whose reads all stand. The keys are now resolved before they decide.

## Measurements (Sprite, cold process, `check packages/cli`)

| | |
|---|---|
| unchanged | 379–403 ms |
| one body edit | ~30,000 ms |
| `lower` | ~7,000 ms |
| held | 493/499 |

These fixes do not move that number: the whole-file read that still un-holds the four command files is propagated through `settle_run` → `settle_reads` → `kept_verdict`, not `recorded_reads`.

## What remains

The per-declaration `Lowered`/settlement answer (DB 07 e/f) plus the Unit codec — the slice that turns the one-edit check into tens of ms.

## Verification

Draft pending Sprite verification: compiler build, `fmt --check` on the changed files, `gate_changed --no-keepers` over affected packages, and `avra test packages/std-avrac`.

body:
## Why

The watcher moved exactly **one** state — green + mergeable + unqueued — and silently skipped every other, so ~19 of 22 open PRs sat forever. Real damage: **#546 sat 17 hours CLEAN with `test: SUCCESS` and `autoMergeRequest=null`** — a push drops auto-merge, `auto-merge.yml` is SKIPPED on `synchronize`, and nothing re-armed it. Nine conflicts, six drafts and three blocked PRs were invisible.

Based on **#551 (`noloop`)**, which is not on `main`, so this branch carries that commit and is rebased onto current `origin/main` (unstacked, base `main`).

## What

Every open PR now draws a real action or a loud name — **never silence**:

- **CLEAN, mergeable, unqueued** → arm auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto --squash`) or enqueue when already armed, under the queue cap.
- **DRAFT** → always named (`#N is a DRAFT — unlandable`), including the conflicting/blocked ones the old draft rule never reached; a green, otherwise-landable one is taken ready unless its title says `DO NOT MERGE` (#338/#339).
- **CONFLICT** → named once with the rebase owed (`git rebase --onto origin/main main <branch>`). Words are one definition shared with `tools/queue_keeper.sh`; the watcher also yields to a standing keeper conflict comment, so there is **one** conflict-commenter.
- **BLOCKED** → names the check it waits on, once.
- An in-queue PR, or a state already named to this head, gets a `note` — never skipped.

Dedup is by `(pr, head, reason)` in the state file plus the comment's own HTML marker, so an unchanged head repeats nothing even with state lost.

## The cap: 3 → 6

`AVRA_QUEUE_MAX` was 3, chosen when a train paid a **cold compiler rebuild** in `prepare` (~7–16 min) and three saturated the runner pool. That rationale is gone — `prepare` now fetches a release compiler (~76 s). This repo's merge-queue ruleset allows **`max_entries_to_build: 10`** concurrent `merge_group` runs (GitHub's setting ranges **1–100**; `max_entries_to_merge: 5`), so 6 stays under the build concurrency and leaves room for entries an owner or the keeper adds. The comment now states the cost the number tracks so the next person re-tunes from data. The workflow no longer hard-codes its own 3 — one source of truth, the code default. No other repo code hard-codes a lower bound.

## Receipts

- `python3 tools/pr_watcher.py --self-test` — 18 plan scenarios plus dedup, never-silent and conflict-yield cases.
- Each new rule **witnessed failing** by breaking the behaviour it guards: arming, draft naming, draft readying, conflict naming, blocked naming, reason dedup, conflict yield, and the 6-default.
- `make -s keepers-static` — clean; `make -s tool-witnesses` — clean.
- A live `--dry-run` over all 23 open PRs: every one named or acted on.
title: ci: the watcher acts on every PR state, and its cap tracks the train's cost

## The gap this closes

The DB 07 ticket (`avra-8sb5.57.176`) states its acceptance as: *"the owner can run `sh tools/warm_edit_bench.sh` — unchanged check packages/cli <= 60 ms, one body edit <= 300 ms (goal 150), cold process, no daemon."* **That script did not exist.** `grep -rn warm_edit Makefile .github/workflows/` answered zero hits: nothing ran it, no keeper, no CI job. So the number it describes could be neither proved nor refuted — and the measured reality (~283 ms unchanged, ~21 350 ms for one body edit) stood with nothing to fail.

This lands the script the ticket names, makes it a **budget** (a hard ceiling, not a printout), and wires it as a keeper.

## The gate

`tools/warm_edit_bench.sh` measures, on a warm store and a fresh `build/avra` process each time (`check packages/cli`):

- **(a) UNCHANGED** — the least of `SPEED_ROUNDS` (3) warm checks, so the first cold round cannot set the price.
- **(b) ONE BODY EDIT** — the least of 3 rounds, each a **fresh nonce edit** of one string literal in one body (`packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av`, `· memo`), never a store hit.

It prints `host <key>`, `warm unchanged <ms>`, `warm edit <ms>`, judges them, and **exits nonzero** when a ceiling is exceeded — naming each by **how much**.

**One budget, not a second one.** The ceilings live in `tools/speed.budget` (the file `tools/speed_ratchet.py` already owns) as two `warm` rows, and the judge is `speed_ratchet.py --warm --raw` — the one reader of that file. The measurement mechanism is `tools/db_measure/warm_edit.sh`'s (a `check --time`, a fresh nonce body edit, wall ms).

| scenario (`check packages/cli`) | ceiling | goal |
|---|---|---|
| unchanged | **60 ms** | 40 ms |
| one body edit | **300 ms** | 150 ms |

## What main measures vs the budget

On the lane's Sprite (`linux-x86-64-amd-epyc`), branch = `origin/main` @ `1240f5af` (this PR adds only tooling):

```
host linux-x86-64-amd-epyc
warm unchanged 283
warm edit 21352
speed: FAIL: warm unchanged: 283ms vs ceiling 60ms, goal 40ms (over by 223ms)
speed: FAIL: warm edit: 21352ms vs ceiling 300ms, goal 150ms (over by 21052ms)
speed: REFUSED — 2 warm scenario(s) past the ceiling or unjudged
```

Second run (via `make warm-edit`, the keeper path): `290 ms` / `21493 ms` — same verdict. **The gate fails loudly on main today, which is the point.** (This matches the DB 07 lane's independent recon: 374–635 ms unchanged, 21 819 ms one edit.)

## Wiring

- **Makefile** — `warm-edit` target (`speed_ratchet.py --self-test`, then the script); added to **`KEEPERS_A`** and **`KEEPERS_PR`**, exactly as `speed-ratchet` is. No `checks.yml` edit is needed — the keepers jobs run `make keepers-a` / `keepers-pr`, which read those lists.
- **Cold path** — a runner with no `.avra-cache` (the `avra-build` artifact carries none) **SKIPS with a word**: `skip cold-store` and a stderr note, exit 0. Never a silent pass. A host with a warm store but no ceiling row says `NO WARM CEILING ROW … NOT GATED`.
- **macOS** — delegates the measurement to the lane's Sprite (`tools/work run`), as `speed-ratchet` does.

## Verification

- `speed_ratchet.py --self-test` — 21 fixtures, including the warm family: hard ceiling (`61 > 60` fails, says `over by 1ms`), `300 == 300` passes, a budget row no round measured is a verdict over nothing, a measured scenario with no ceiling is unrecorded, the two families share one budget and never judge each other, another host is not gated, and the round trip carries warm rows.
- `make speed-ratchet` — still passes: `8 phase(s) within the ceiling` (the warm rows are filtered out of the phase gate).
- `make keepers-static` — clean.
- `make warm-edit` — fails loudly on the Sprite with the numbers above (the intended state); exits 2 through make.
- `sh tools/warm_edit_bench.sh` with `SPEED_LOCAL=1` and no store — prints `skip cold-store`, exit 0.
title: ci: the DB 07 warm-edit gate — the ticket's own script, wired as a keeper

body:
# one generation: can gen-2 be eliminated? — the measured answer

**Question (owner, 2026-10-10).** The cold path was measured at ~1050 s:
C objects 10 s, seed link (`make recover`) 58 s, gen-1 `make avra` 517 s,
gen-2 `make avra` 514 s — the two self-compiles are 95% of it. Is gen-2
*always* necessary, or only when the compiler's own source moved in a
way that affects codegen? If a train's diff touches no compiler path,
`tools/compiler_paths.sh` says so; maybe the second build is provably
redundant.

**Answer. No for a stale seed, and yes for an unchanged one — and the
unchanged case is already exploited.** Gen-2 is required whenever the
standing compiler's source differs from the tree's. It is not required
when they are the same: a compiler built from the tree's own source is
reused with **zero** builds (the CI exact-key cache and `work`'s
`.avra-compiler-hash` warm check), and a fixed point rebuilt on the same
machine is **byte-identical** to itself.

## The experiment (one Sprite, cold, no cache)

`origin/main` @ `6ddb4391`; the worktree's compiler source equals main's
pushed artifact, so the run reused main's compiler with **0 builds**.
Then, on that Sprite:

| step | what it is | time |
|---|---|---|
| `recover` | link the committed seed | 57 s |
| gen-1 | the seed compiles the source | 880 s |
| gen-2 | gen-1 compiles the source again | 856 s |

Whole-file SHA-256 and `.text`-section SHA-256 of every compiler, then
`cmp`:

| pair | result |
|---|---|
| gen-1 vs gen-2 | **differ, 11,644,429 bytes** (first at byte 42) |
| gen-2 vs an independent rebuild of the tree on the same Sprite (from main's compiler) | **byte-identical** (whole file, `.text`, build id) |
| main's compiler vs that rebuild | differ only because they were built on **different machines** |

The unchanged case, directly: from the gen-2 fixed point, `make avra`
(~845 s) produced a binary **byte-identical** to the one it rebuilt
(whole file and `.text`); a further build hit the compiler's own store
and finished in 1 s. So a compiler whose source is the tree's rebuilds
itself unchanged.

**Why gen-1 ≠ gen-2.** The generation law: a change to lowering or memory
reaches a compiler's own body only when a compiler already carrying it
compiles that body. The committed seed's source *lags* the tree
(`bootstrap/seed.sources` ≠ `tools/sources_hash.sh`), so gen-1's own body
was laid out by the seed's older codegen and gen-2's by the source's own.
Gen-2 is the compiler this source emits; gen-1 is a different compiler.
No skip is safe while the seed's codegen may lag — this is the law, not
slack.

**Where reuse already pays.** A compiler built from the tree's exact
source needs no build: the CI cache is keyed by
`tools/compiler_paths.sh --key` and `work`'s warm check is
`.avra-compiler-hash == compiler_hash`. The measured run reused main's
artifact with zero builds. The only gap was `make bootstrap`, which
always did two builds even when the seed already IS the tree.

## The change

- `tools/seed_is_tree.sh` — the decision: given the tree's source hash
  and the seed's recorded hash, answer `seed` or `twice`. Empty or
  unequal never answers `seed`. Self-tested (5 cases) and run by `make
  tool-witnesses` (a train keeper).
- `make bootstrap` — when the seed IS this tree, stop at `recover` (no
  self-compile); otherwise the two builds stand.
- `bootstrap/README.md` — the law and the measurements.

## Before / after (cold, real CI shape)

- **Seed lags the tree (main today: seed `77a75ecc`, tree `59a2c686`):**
  unchanged at 2 self-compiles — **~1050 s** on the CI runner (the
  reported figure), 1793 s on this Sprite.
- **Seed IS the tree:** `make bootstrap` finishes in the `recover` step
  alone — **~58 s**, no self-compile (Sprite probe: 110 s `recover`,
  output `bootstrap: the seed IS this tree — no self-compile`, and the
  recovered compiler emitted the same module as the fixed point).

The fast path fires only while nothing under `tools/sources_hash.sh` has
moved since the seed refresh (the seed identity includes tests, which
`compiler_paths.sh --key` deliberately leaves out), so it is narrower
than the source-key reuse above. A follow-up that makes the seed record
the compiler-source key would widen it; that changes the seed identity
and is left out deliberately.

The 2-minute CI goal still wants a faster `lower` (DB 07) or a fresh
seed; generation-skipping cannot halve the stale-seed cold path.
title: bootstrap: a seed that IS the tree skips the self-compile

body:
The deterministic watcher (#539) enqueued EVERY green, mergeable PR with no depth limit. Each queue entry spawns its own ~40 min train, so a full queue saturates the shared runner pool and the pipeline runs SLOWER: the queue grew 3 -> 8 within twenty minutes of landing.

## Fix
In `tools/pr_watcher.py`'s pure `plan()`:
1. **Depth cap** — rule (b) enqueues only while the merge queue holds fewer than `AVRA_QUEUE_MAX` entries (default **3**). A green PR over the cap is held and named (`queue at 3 — holding #537`), never dropped; a later pass enqueues it when a slot frees.
2. **Order preserved** — candidates are taken in the order the list arrives (no re-sort/shuffle), so whatever priority the pass carries is the order the cap spends.
3. **Running trains untouched** — running entries count against the depth budget and are never dequeued; rule (c)'s existing `stuck` predicate still only kicks entries with no train, so a re-enqueue never displaces an in-flight train.

Rationale recorded beside `QUEUE_MAX` in code and in the workflow header: N full trains in flight saturate the runners, so more entries land slower, not more.

## Proof
- `python3 tools/pr_watcher.py --self-test` — 13 plan scenarios including `queue-at-cap-holds` (zero enqueue), `room-below-cap-enqueues`, `cap-holds-the-excess` (names what it held), `running-entry-untouched` (no churn), plus the cap-log, `AVRA_QUEUE_MAX` and why-mark assertions.
- Live `--dry-run` against `avra-lang/avra` while the queue was 9 deep: `hold 524 queue at 3 — holding #524`, summary `queue at 9/3, 1 held` — the cap held a green PR instead of adding a tenth entry.
- Later dry-run once every green non-draft PR had already been queued: `queue at 11/3: 0 new enqueue(s), 0 held, 8 stuck-entry kick(s)`. The cap's new enqueues and rule (c)'s kicks now wear distinct marks (`[new]` / `[kick]`), so the dry run cannot be misread as the cap flooding.

No `.av` changed; `make keepers-static` green.
title: ci: the watcher caps the merge queue at three entries

body:
## What

Supersedes #522, whose per-callee-type fold was RED by design: a fn value's
address was grouped by the register it was minted at — the code lane's `int`
— while a `CallPtr` folded that same `int`, and a capture-free fn's static code
address was filed under a node no call reached. Two cases failed on #522
(`code_hash_test.av:74`, `:92`).

This lands #522's work (the 37 per-family entry fns, `family_code_hash` and the
per-type fold) with the reach repaired:

- an `FnAddr` is grouped by the **box** it is pushed into (slot 0) — the fn type
  a `CallPtr` sees, never the code lane's `int`;
- a `StaticAddr` of a box of code (a named fn used as a value) is grouped by the
  read's own type;
- a `CallPtr` folds the **box at seat 0**, not the slot-0 code read;
- the fallback node still holds every address, so an unknown box stays sound.

## Proof (Mac, warm `make try`)

- `code_hash_test.av`: **`25/28` before, `28/28` after**. The two parked cases
  at `:74` and `:92` pass, and a new attack at `:98` — a fn handed through a
  cell the caller passes on — is witnessed failing without the fix and passing
  with it.
- `meta_test.av` 10/10.
- `gate_changed --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers` clean; `make
  keepers-static` clean; `make keepers-pr` clean.

## What remains

Precision for the compiler's own families: `ask()` dispatches through the shared
`verify: fn(int)->int`, so all 37 verifiers pool under one fn type and a verifier
edit still moves 36 family rows. That is DB 07 A11 — rows and buckets as named
parts of their producer's answer, dissolving the family dispatch into direct
