body:
## The `compiler` step on a cache miss

Measured cold on a Sprite (no `build/`, no cache), one tree, seconds:

| step | at -O1 | at -O0 |
|---|---|---|
| C objects (`COMPILER_OBJS`) | 10 | 10 |
| seed link (`make recover`, 44 MB `seed.ll`) | 58 | 9 |
| gen-1 `make avra` | 517 | — |
| gen-2 `make avra` | 514 | — |

The **two self-compiles are ~95%** of the step. The seed link is 5%, the C objects 1%. So `-O0` on the seed, caching the seed binary, or caching the objects cannot move the number. The seed link is also only paid on a *bootstrap* (no reachable `avrac-*` cache); a normal miss restores a compiler and runs `make avra && make avra`, no seed at all.

Cold self-compile phase split (`./avra build packages/cli --time`, 508 s):

```
parse 24  analyze 39  lower 368  keep 54  emit 43  link 2.5
```

`lower` is one program and is the whole cost.

## What the fix does

Cache `.avra-cache` (the compiler's store) with `build/avra`. A store is one compiler's, so the restored binary reads its own store for the first self-compile. Measured, same tree, a real source change:

| | gen-1 | gen-2 | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| today (binary only) | 517 | 514 | 1031 |
| fix (binary + store) | **404** | 516 | **920** |

The analysis and emit rows reuse; `lower` still re-runs. The **second** self-compile is the new compiler's own first build and is cold whatever the cache does — the generation law needs it.

## Why most trains miss, and the churn

**A cache is scope-bound.** A run restores caches from its own branch and `main`; never a sibling's or a child's ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/caching-dependencies-to-speed-up-workflows)). Each merge-queue train stands on its own throwaway ref `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-<n>-<sha>`, so a compiler a train saves is unreachable to every other train (and to `main`). The live census:

- 2310 caches / 4.28 GB
- 782 `avrac-*` compiler caches, **120 on `main`, ~660 on unreachable merge refs**
- 1149 `speed-main-*` + 170 `queue-keeper-*`, all tiny, almost all on merge refs
- 1080 MB of the 4.28 GB is merge-scoped and unreachable to any other run

So every train rebuilds; only a `push` to `main` writes a compiler the next train can read. This is why 45/51 of the last completed `compiler` steps are misses.

`push` and `workflow_dispatch` alone may write the default branch's scope, so this saves there and nowhere else. That stops the ~1150 `speed-*` and ~660 `avrac-*` junk entries per wave from churning the useful `main` caches toward eviction.

## Is it getting worse?

No. 51 completed `compiler` steps in order, seconds (0 = exact hit/skip):

```
945 944 452 954 945 606 958 945 592 977 617 665 770 976 946 310 616 481
939 958 942 946 429 387 310 949 0 0 614 0 671 937 0 942 957 620 689 963
930 732 972 955 971 985 0 469 956 943 408
```

median **937 s**, mean 761 s, max 985 s. First-half mean **771 s**, second-half mean **750 s** — flat. It is bimodal: exact hits at 0 s and misses pinned near the 15–16 min ceiling. Both a 310 s and a 937 s miss did exactly the same two `make avra` builds with no bootstrap — the spread is runner/host variance, not tree growth.

## What this does not reach

The owner's 2–5 min target is not reachable by caching. A miss needs one full self-compilation by the new compiler (`lower` alone is 368 s), and no artifact cache removes it — the store is per-compiler by design. Getting there wants either a faster `lower` or a proof that one generation suffices; both are compiler changes, recorded here rather than guessed at.

## Checks

- `gate_changed --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers`: `nothing changed — no .av, no affected package`
- `make keepers-static`: clean
- `make keepers-pr`: clean
- workflow YAML parses
title: ci: the compiler cache carries its store, and only main-scoped saves cross runs

Pins the same-arity half of the kept-instantiation key's shape fold: two records differing only in one field's type must name different keys, so a shape moved under the same name never reads an old instance.

## Context
The core fix for avra-8sb5.57.264 already landed (#458): a roaming instantiation keeps its code facts under `inst_key_of(home object key, argument shapes, symbol)`, so a query reaching a held generic is hashed instead of going absent. avra-8sb5.57.266 landed with #470 (unknown symbols read absent; runtime rows are name-hashed). `tools/code_hash_attacks.sh` is already wired into the train's `cache-attacks` job, and `held-dyn` passes on main.

## This change
`code_hash_test`'s `inst_key_of` spec covered `int` vs `record 1 (int)`. This adds the sharper case: `record 2 (int, int)` vs `record 2 (int, string)` — same arity, same first field, one field's type moved.

## Why not an end-to-end attack
An end-to-end held-generic shape attack cannot isolate the shape field: the caller's own lowered body tracks the argument type's shape, so the query recomputes whether or not the instance key folds shapes (witnessed: with `Instance.shapes` forced empty the scenario still recomputes). The key fold is the unit spec's to pin; the end-to-end `held-dyn` attack pins the held-instance path.

Receipt: `code_hash_test` 28/28 (Sprite); `fmt --check` clean; `make idioms` no new violations; `make keepers-static` clean.

## Why

A PR runs the minimum, so `cache-attacks` is skipped on every PR and only runs on
a train. A store-layout rewrite (DB 05 stage 2, #524) therefore went **PR-green**
and then failed **every train it entered** — four consecutive trains at
`f5d4d2e5`/`9de2e3eb`/`60d21af1`/`4ebc31d9`, each with the identical seven
failures:

```
FAIL  kr: a cold check records no run of held.av reading mid.av ('')
FAIL  kv: a cold check records held.av's runs as '', top.av's as '', alone.av's as ''
FAIL  no Unit family directory under .avra-cache: bin / obj / store
FAIL  a compiler of other bytes wrote into another's store
FAIL  nr: no record row places nrl's file, so the removal attacks nothing
FAIL  nr: nrl's record is gone — user keys on nrl's bytes and re-reads
FAIL  avra explain moved the store
cache-attacks: 334 builds through one store, 113 under a hold, 7 failed
```

The attacks read the *old* store's on-disk files (`.avra-cache/*/rows`, a
`unit/` family directory, one store per compiler). The new store keeps its
values in a sealed pack, so those probes read nothing. Because #524 sits at
position 1 in the merge queue and its own required check never runs the attacks,
the queue cannot drain: #524 fails a train, drops, the watcher re-enqueues it,
and the cycle repeats.

## What

Name the attacks where the cache can move:

- **main's own push** now runs `cache-attacks` (it was skipped), so a store
  change main has just taken is named on `main`, not only one train later.
- **a PR whose diff reaches** the compiler's `store/`, its cache key files
  (`build.av`, `record.av`, `answers.av`, `host/input.av`, `lower/code_hash.av`)
  or the attack scripts now runs them — the gap that let #524 through.
- The plan forces `build=1` when the attacks are owed, since they need a
  compiler and its objects; `prepare` builds and hands down `avra-build` on
  push too.

Verified the trigger fires exactly on the store/cache paths:
`#524 7a2f7dad -> cache=1`, `#537 43e5956e (record.av) -> cache=1`,
`#536 92d2ec21 -> cache=0`, `#527 1a6c9bc5 -> cache=0`, `main fe4ed90 -> cache=0`.

## Receipts

- `make keepers-static` — clean
- `make keepers-pr` — clean (`attack: 23 survivor(s), all in the baseline`)
- `sh tools/gate_changed.sh --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers` — `nothing changed — no .av, no affected package`
- `yaml.safe_load` parses; the job graph is unchanged on a cache-less PR

This does **not** make #524 pass — its own branch must still update
`tools/cache_attacks.sh` for the packed layout and stop `avra explain` writing
to the store. This change means the next such PR is caught on the PR, and the
attacks are held on `main`.

## Why

Every train's `keepers-a` job failed mid-run — the runtime keepers held to
a clock (`runtime-tests`, `runtime-mutations`) ran first in that job and the
runner was killed during the ~11-minute mutation run, so the job never
reached the first keeper half.

The `a program: native != expected` lines in those logs are NOT a failure:
they are `runtime/tests/verdict_test.c`'s expected program tests
(`two_tasks_print` prints `b\na` where `a\nb` is wanted; `deadlocks` traps
with exit 2), and the suite reports `verdict: 31 checks, 0 failed` on every
run, green and red alike.

## What

1. **`keepers-a` no longer runs the runtime keepers** (`make keepers-alone`).
   It runs the first keeper half alone, which now passes on the train.
   A standalone runtime-keepers job with a bounded process count is a
   follow-up; the Makefile's `make keepers` still holds them.
2. **`memcap.sh` fixes its own cap.** It keyed the cap on a process group
   that a tty-less shell never gave the guarded job: dash answers `set -m`
   with "job control turned off", the job keeps the caller's pgid, and
   `tree_rss` matched no process — a 500 MB hog passed a 300 MB cap on the

   has a group of its own.
3. **`mutations.py` bounds each test's output**: to a 16 MiB file
   (`RLIMIT_FSIZE`, SIGXFSZ ends a runaway) with only the head read back,
   and kills the run's process group past `BOUND`. `capture_output` held

- `memcap --self-test`: 2 fixtures, and a 500 MB hog is killed at 511 MB

body:
Deterministic, no LLM. Three mechanisms and the PR floor.

## 1. The deterministic watcher (P0)
`tools/pr_watcher.py` + `.github/workflows/pr-watcher.yml`, every 2 minutes and after every `checks` run. A pure `plan()` (proved by `--self-test`) decides; only `collect`/`execute` touch GitHub.

- (a) a PR whose required `test` FAILED: comment the exact `job - line` and re-run failed jobs **once**;
- (b) a green + mergeable + unmerged PR: enqueue (auto-merge if unset, direct enqueue if set);
- (c) a queue entry **stuck** (>5 min old with no `merge_group` run since it was enqueued): dequeue + re-enqueue;
- (d) a failed train: name the failing `job - line` on the PR.

**Three defects from the first live pass are fixed:**
1. One action's `gh` error no longer aborts the pass — each action is in its own try, a failure logs `pr-watcher: <pr> <do> FAILED — <err>`, the rest run.
2. Rule (c) no longer churns the queue — `stuck` reads the entry's `enqueuedAt` and fires ONLY when it is >5 min old with no run created for it since. A fresh entry, or one whose train is running, is never touched.
3. State is committed and saved in a `finally`, with only SUCCEEDED actions' marks — a failed action is retried, a succeeded one is not repeated.

## 2. PR check = minimum + cache, over the affected closure
`checks.yml`: a PR runs fmt on its changed `.av`, and `avra check` over the packages the diff **affects** — touched plus every package that reaches one (`tools/affected_packages.sh`, the same ONE definition the train uses). No keepers, no suites, no object build; `--pr-minimum` in `gate_changed.sh` skips the wasm proof. So a change in A that breaks a dependent B's compile refuses on the PR, not a train (#484).

## 3. Auto-enqueue on PR open
`.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`: opened / ready_for_review / synchronize / reopened -> `gh pr merge --auto --squash`, skipped for drafts and forks.

## Measured proofs
- Watcher `--self-test`: **9 plan scenarios + 3 defect cases** (healthy queue -> zero actions; a failed action does not stop the pass; state saves only succeeded marks). Live `--dry-run` over the real repo: 17 actions, **0 dequeue/re-enqueue**.
- Affected-closure refusal (draft #542, since closed): a rename in `std-compress` left `std-http_compress` broken. Touched-only floor **exit 0** (the bug); affected floor **exit 1**, refusing `packages/std-http_compress`: `@std.compress does not export decoded`. After fixing B, **exit 0**.
- PR floor timing (real CI): a tests-only PR touching `packages/std-path` ran the whole check in **86 s** (prepare 40 s, gate 40 s, `test` 2 s). The affected-closure run of #542's fix: **85 s** (06:27:54 -> 06:29:19). Both under 2 min with the warm compiler cache.
- Auto-enqueue: this PR's `auto-merge` run enabled auto-merge the instant it opened and the queue took it; a draft PR's auto-merge run was correctly skipped.

**Token note:** this repo's `GITHUB_TOKEN` auto-merge DID start a `merge_group` run, so `auto-merge.yml` works with the default token. The workflows prefer `secrets.AVRA_QUEUE_TOKEN` when present, for the watcher's direct enqueue path.

(`make pr-watcher` targets were dropped from this PR to keep it off the compiler path — run `python3 tools/pr_watcher.py --self-test` / `--dry-run`.)
title: ci: a deterministic watcher, auto-enqueue, and a two-minute PR floor

`.218` part 2. A compile-time run's record now names, per read file, the DECLARATION it read (`RunRead { path, digest, ref, print }`), not just the file. A key folds the declaration's write-time syntax while the read file's text moved but a declaration may still name the same syntax; `resolve_pending_reads` finalizes that hold decision inside `settle_holds`, after the walk, never inside a key. So a body edit ELSEWHERE in a file a run read leaves its readers held, while editing the declaration the run read reads them in the first attempt.

Measured, full-package (`packages/cli`, fresh store, ONE comment-only edit to `packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/record.av`):

| compiler | held |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` (base) | **490/497** |
| branch, before the fix | **0/497** |
| branch, with the fix | **490/497** |

The pre-fix 0 was a decode bug: `read_wire` writes four cells joined by `~`, and a plain read (no ref, no print) ends `hexpath~hexdigest~~`. `split` DROPS a run's trailing empties, so the decoder read four cells as two and refused the whole `file` line (`xs.length != 4`). The file was then unplaced in `places_of`, which `home_moved` read as a home whose text moved — every full-package check turned four times and ended holding nothing. The decoder now reads the cells by PADDING to four, so a written-empty cell arrives empty; the round trip is pinned in `run_reads_test.av` for a plain read, a held declaration's read, and one with every cell empty.

Receipts:
- `CACHE_ATTACKS=kr,kv,tw sh tools/cache_attacks.sh` — 22 builds through one store, 7 under a hold, **0 failed** (`tw` is the two-edit attack).
- `./avra test packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/run_reads_test.av` — **6/6**.
- `tools/gate_changed.sh --files … --packages std-avrac --no-keepers` — clean (fmt + idioms).
- `make keepers-static` and `make keepers-pr` — clean.

body:
## What

The hard per-phase speed ratchet. The only speed guard today is `tools/speed_note.sh` (#478) — a **soft** per-JOB 25% *warning*, so a sum of small per-phase regressions slips through (cold `keep` went 2.7 s → 44–62 s exactly this way, with no single PR crossing the line).

This holds each **phase** of `packages/cli`'s own build and check against a ceiling and **REFUSES** past it (non-zero exit, the phase named with its ceiling and its measured ms).

- **`tools/speed_measure.sh`** — a warm one-edit build and check. Each round appends a fresh nonce so a round is never a store hit; the **least** of `SPEED_ROUNDS` (3) per phase is the price. A cold store **skips** with a word (the first rounds would be the whole program's price, not the phase's).
- **`tools/speed_ratchet.py`** — the gate. Ceilings live in **`tools/speed.budget`**, keyed per machine (`platform-machine-cpu`) so a Mac, a Sprite and a runner are never compared. `--accept` lowers a ceiling to what was measured and **never raises one**; raising one is a human edit and that diff is the review. Fixtures prove the gate before it judges (`--self-test`).
- **`Makefile`** — `speed-ratchet` and `speed-accept`, in **`KEEPERS_A`** and **`KEEPERS_PR`**.

## The budgets (recorded on a Sprite, `linux-x86-64-amd-epyc`, the checks' image)

| command | phase | ceiling (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| build | analyze | 1742 |
| build | lower | 2491 |
| build | keep | **6704** |
| build | emit | 983 |
| build | link | 1829 |
| check | analyze | 1768 |
| check | lower | 2568 |
| check | keep | 6835 |

Tolerance: **1.25× + 250 ms** per phase. A wall-clock phase on a Sprite moves ~20% session to session (measured), so a tighter ratio would flake; the least-of-rounds removes outliers, and 25% still catches the cited 16× cold-`keep` regression and any real per-phase rise.

## Demonstrated failing

A throwaway `sleep(ms(3000))` in the compiler's `kept` hot path (`derive.av`), built and measured on a Sprite:

```
speed: FAIL: build keep: 9858ms vs ceiling 6704ms (limit 8630ms)
speed: FAIL: check keep: 9829ms vs ceiling 6835ms (limit 8794ms)
speed: REFUSED — 2 phase(s) past the ceiling or unjudged:
speed:   build keep: 9858ms vs ceiling 6704ms (limit 8630ms)
speed:   check keep: 9829ms vs ceiling 6835ms (limit 8794ms)
```

Exit 1. The regression was reverted; the clean tree gates:

```
speed: clean — 8 phase(s) within the ceiling
```

## Like-for-like, and where it runs

- On the **Mac** the measurement goes to the lane's **Sprite** (`tools/work run`), so a loaded Mac supplies no number. `make speed-ratchet` / `make keepers-pr` on a lane therefore block on the Sprite.
- In **CI** the keepers jobs start with a **cold store** (`.avra-cache` is not in the `avra-build` artifact) and a runner whose CPU is not the Sprite's, so the keeper **skips with a word** rather than flaking the train. Recording a runner row (a human edit of `tools/speed.budget`) is how CI would gate too.

## Open PRs this would flag (once measured on a Sprite)

Any lane touching the compiler's analyze/lower/keep/emit/link hot paths and regressing one phase by >25%: the store/DB lanes (**#509, #524, #516, #494, #484, #504, #487**), the flow/task lanes (**#527, #529, #528, #525, #510**), the nodes lanes (**#534, #535**), the family-code-hash lane (**#522**), and #531's per-family dispatch. They will be flagged when their lane runs `make keepers-pr` on its Sprite (or `make speed-ratchet`).

## Gate

- `gate_changed.sh --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers`: clean (no `.av`, no package touched)
- `make keepers-static`: clean
- `make keepers-pr`: clean — including `speed-ratchet 193s`, `8 phase(s) within the ceiling`

body:
DB07a: each family's verifier is now a DIRECT call, not a `fn(int)->int` value in `Kernel.verifiers`.

**Before:** `Kernel.verified()` dispatched through `self.verifiers.get()[family]` which was a `List\<Verifier.By(fn(int)->int)\>`. Under the code hash, every `CallPtr` site folds all fns whose address is taken — all 37 verifier closures. Changing one verifier contaminated every family's code hash.

**After:** `Verifier.By` drops its fn payload. The kernel holds a SINGLE `by_dispatch: Cell\<fn(int,int)->int\>` that the workspace sets to a generated match over `Family.all()`. Each arm is a DIRECT call to a named verifier, so a `CallPtr` fold reaches only the dispatcher.

**Changes:**
- `kernel.av`: `Verifier.By` → no payload; `Kernel.by_dispatch` added; `verified()` calls dispatcher; `family()` takes no arg; `set_verify()` for tests

## What it does

- `within limit { body }` lowers as a ONE-TURN LOOP whose end is the scope's own landing. The scope opens INSIDE the turn and its end is a `Deferral.Landing` at that frame, so a `return` or a `?` out of the body still runs it, exactly as a `defer` there would — and an unwind is caught AT its own landing, not by the fn's cold exit. `features/tasks/lower.av`; `LowerCx.within_loops` and `WithinMark` (`features/contract.av`); `open_landing`/`close_landing` (`compiler/lower/walk.av`).
- `unwinds()` (`features/emit.av`) jumps to the innermost open `within`'s landing: it runs the frames inside the scope (which run the scope's end and land its answer in the loop's cell) and emits `LoopJump` out of the one-turn loop; with no `within` open it is unchanged (run the frames, `FnExit`).
- The epilogue is the Ok/Err region on the unwind flag: set, the fn leaves unwinding; clear, the body's own answer stands. Ladder 14 flips the Err arm to `Err(TimedOut)` and adds the `landed`-cell pass-through. **`within` still answers its block as written** — no user-visible behaviour changes here.

Ladder 15 of FLOW 03 (`docs/2026_10_06_FLOW_03_DESIGN.md` §3.1/§3.2/§3.8, §4 step 15, ticket `avra-8sb5.34.53.24`).

## What it does
- A `while` back-edge carries one check: `FlagRead(RtFlag.Tick)` (an ATOMIC load) and, taken, one call to `avra_tick_cold` (the cold side). A `for` over a list or a range carries none. The atomic load is what stops `-O2` hoisting the tick out of a counted loop, matching the runtime's `__atomic_load_n(..., RELAXED)`.
- `avra_tick_cold` fires due timers, checks the running task's own deadline, raises a standing cancel and yields when others are ready. `avra_vtask_tick_cold` is its twin over the evaluator's virtual task; the seeded countdown (`tick_turn_comes`) is ONE definition both call, so both engines draw the same turn.
- `@unbroken` fns' own `while`s carry no check (decided by the cancel pass's `spins` bit); a lifted lambda wears its maker's law.
- A compile-time run emits no check; a program the cancel pass says links no scheduler emits none either. WHETHER A SCHEDULER IS LINKED is settled by the DRIVER (`Program.lowered_bodies`) before lowering: the members' settled bits plus the ENTRY ROOT's own top-level waits (`file_links_scheduler`), because the root is no declaration and the pass cannot see it. A wasm build emits no check whatever the survey says (its runtime has no fiber).
- `avra_tick_cold` returns at once inside an evaluated run, so the compiler's own back-edges never draw from a guest's schedule.

## Fixes since 9c4aafc (adversarial review)
1. **BLOCKER — the entry root's waits.** A program whose only `spawn`/`avra_fiber_sleep` is at TOP LEVEL emitted no check. `members_link_scheduler` + `Program.root_links` survey the root now; `wait_links`/`call_links` read a runtime row's own column. PROVEN: `spin_top` (top-level spawn + top-level `while`) is `eval == native == expected` under a seed; the backedge IR test counts the top-level `= flag tick`.
2. **MEDIUM — the tick load is atomic** (`avra_llvm_build_load_atomic`, `LLVMAtomicOrderingMonotonic`), so `-O2` cannot hoist it.
3. **MEDIUM — mutations for every new C line** (`g_runs` guard, the `avra_tick_cold` timer/deadline checks, `avra_vtask_tick_cold`, `within_opened`'s `wanted` store), each killed by a new `tick_test` case.
4. **LOW — `make vocab`'s `RtHost` row** names `hosted` (the exhaustive `row.host` match), not `rt_dispatch`.
5. **#5 confirmed real**: `record_schedulers` was a side effect inside the memoized pass. It is now a DRIVER-side projection (`members_link_scheduler` is pure; `Program.lowered_bodies` sets the one bit), so a query no longer writes it and a reuse cannot read a stale bit.

## MEASURED (Sprite, Linux x86_64, clang 22)
- `spin_top`: `eval == native == expected` (713808895) — the top-level case.
- `spin_seeded`: `eval == native == expected`.
- backedge IR: 6/6; cancel_reach: 28/28.
- `make runtime-tests`: green (new tick cases: due timer at a back-edge, a scope's opening arms the source, a compiled back-edge inside an evaluated run).
- `make runtime-mutations`: **221/221 killed, 0 survived, 0 rotten**.
- `make keepers` WHOLE: **green** (vocab `hosted:128`, footprint clean, ui-board 18 claims over a 100 KB module, witnesses, idioms, runtime-tests/mutations).
- `make try` / `make avra` self-host: builds.

## Unverified / notes
- `flow-gate` (the G1 bench) — the known `.32` deadlock red; #523 (`a cached pid, not getpid`) has now landed, but the row was not re-run here and the baseline was not re-recorded.
- The scheduler survey is a whole-program over-approximation: a fn that reaches through a value can still set a callee's may-reach bit, so some programs link a scheduler they never use at a back-edge (perf, not correctness; wasm is guarded).

## Revision (head e289f802): a join of a cancelled task KEEPS its trap

The earlier head made the compiled `avra_task_join` pass a cancelled task's
cancel to its joiner while the evaluator still refused, so one program answered
two ways: CI's `std-time/tests/cancelled_join` read "native exited clean, wanted
a trap (code 2)". That half is taken out of this rung. A join of a task that
ENDED cancelled traps in both engines, as on main; the pass-through lands with
the evaluator's arm, the caught-await lowering and `main`'s report, in one PR.
Everything else below stands: a cancel reaches an evaluated task's park, a join
its caller's own cancel cut hands back NULL with the bit set, the
`avra_task_join_caught` and `avra_task_ended` rows, the asker on the task.
New: a caller ALREADY unwinding that joins a cancelled task is refused nothing
(NULL, no trap) — `standing_join_of_cancelled`, with its mutation.

MEASURED on the Sprite (avra-reuse, compiler bootstrapped from this tree):
`make runtime-tests` 0 failed (flow 262 checks); `make runtime-mutations`
252 of 252 killed; `avra test packages/std-time` 7/7, 2 refusals + 2 programs
proved; `features/tasks` 36/36, 23 programs; `runtime_reach_test` 3/3.
`make keepers-static` clean on the Mac. Read "`avra_task_join` is trap-free"
and "MEDIUM — engine divergence" below as superseded by this section.

---

Ladder 12's runtime half: an evaluated task hears a cancel at its park, and a
join stops trapping. Hosted `Unhosted`, so this is rung 1 of the THREE-rung
ladder — the row alone, with its C body. The evaluator arm, the Avra
declaration and the caught-await lowering are the following PR (they cannot
gate until the seed is refreshed, since the compiler's own source would
declare the row).

Rebased on `origin/main` after #520 and #526 landed, so the typing commits that
were sitting on #520 are gone and only this slice's runtime work remains. The
`flow-gate` red is the known #519 baseline versus main's `getpid()` tick
regression (`.32`); it is not this change and the baseline is not re-recorded.

## What it does
- **A cancel reaches an evaluated task's park.** `fiber_cancelled` claimed a
  park only for a compiled task (`!(f->legacy && f->virtual)`), so an
  evaluated task's sleep/join stayed deaf. #431 gated that on the evaluator
  not reading the bit; ladder 9 (#499, merged) emits the after-call test and
  the evaluator's `flag_now` reads `avra_vtask_unwinding`
  (`backend/interp.av:1003`). A cancel now claims the park, and `set_claimed`
  sets the evaluated task's own `unwinding` — it has no post-switch
  `cancel_met` to run.
- **`avra_task_join` is trap-free** (D2). A cancelled task's answer does not
  exist, so the join hands back NULL and sets the caller's unwind bit, exactly
  as a cancel the caller's own asker left does; `task_awaited` calls
  `cancel_met` after a cut park.
- **A new row, `avra_task_join_caught`**, hosted `Unhosted`: it waits without
  passing the awaited task's cancel to the caller, and answers a two-cell
  `Cancelled` box (`by`, `at`) or NULL. `avra_task_ended` gains a row for its
  existing C body.
- **A cancel a spawned task meets records its asker.** `task_cancelled` keeps
  `by` on the task's cells, where a caught join reads it: a fiber task ends in
  `fiber_start` and never reaches `task_ended`, so a non-main cancel named
  nobody (`by` was always 0). `avra_fiber.c:2030`.

## Adversarial review — fixes applied
- **HIGH — `Cancelled.by` for a spawned task.** Recorded in `task_cancelled`;
  a new flow case has a non-main task cancel and catch, naming the asker (the
  old `by == 0` case only agreed because main's id is 0).
- **MEDIUM — `avra_task_join_caught` claimed `stood`.** It mints its box, so
  the column is dropped and the `stood` twin returns to 7
  (`runtime_counts_test.av`).
- **MEDIUM — engine divergence on a cancelled join.** The compiled join passes
  the cancel on; the evaluator's `task_join_val` still refuses. The case's name
  says it covers the evaluator alone.
- **LOW — `avra_fiber.h`** no longer says a join is cut and traps.
- **LOW — the `by`/`at` asserts.** `by` is now real; the `at` check reads as
  the placeholder it is (`TASK_SITE` has no writer yet).

## MEASURED
- `make runtime-tests` on the Sprite (rebased tree) — all 20 tests, 0 failed;
  `flow_test` 220 checks, 0 failed.
- `make runtime-mutations` on the Sprite (rebased tree) — 212 of 212 killed,

- `make keepers` WHOLE on the Sprite (rebased tree) — passed, 0 refused.
- `runtime_counts_test.av` 5/5; `features/tasks/tests/tasks_test.av` 19/19.
- `make keepers-static` — clean. `pr-keepers` green on CI.

## Unverified / owed (the rung split)
- The evaluator arm for `avra_task_join_caught`, the Avra declaration and the
  `t.await catch` lowering are rung 2; the row is `Unhosted` until then.
- `Cancelled.at` is 0 natively: the record carries the site cell but nothing

- The evaluator's `task_join_val` still traps on a cancelled task, where the
  compiled join passes the cancel on (rung 2 flips it).
- `main`'s cancelled end (defer`s run, one stderr line, exit 1) is rung 2.

Ladder 11 + 13 of FLOW 03 (design `docs/2026_10_06_FLOW_03_DESIGN.md` §3.9, §4 steps 11+13, §5).

## What it does

- `within limit { body }` is now the TASKS feature's own expression, a head that keeps its brace, exactly as `if` and `while` do — `"within" l:expression b:block` with `@head(l)` (`features/tasks/mod.av`). `limit` is read at its own `ms` field once, so one field read serves typing and lowering; the printer spells the written span back, never the read (`compiler/format/source_text.av`).
- The block stays INLINE. Lowering opens the task's deadline scope (`avra_fiber_within`), registers its end through the frame (`call_at_exit`), lowers the body block, and closes — so `return` and `?` out of the body still run the scope end, exactly as a `defer` there would. `features/tasks/lower.av`, `check.av`, `node.av`, `semantics.av`.
- `@std/time` LOSES the `within` component and its two externs; it KEEPS `Duration` and gains `TimedOut { after: Duration, at: List<Frame> }` and `late<T>(t) -> Result<T, TimedOut>` (§3.9's catch fold, used by nothing yet — ladder 14's flip).
- The keyword sweep: `within` removed from 47 `use @std.time.{…}` lists across `packages/` and `tools/`, and the compiler's own identifiers named `within` renamed by the predecessor's sweep commit.
- New `Expr.Within` node: every exhaustive `Expr` dispatch paid (`core/nodes.av`, `core/store.av`, `features/code.av`, `features/dispatch.av`, `compiler/references.av`, `compiler/node_waits.av`, the printer).

# DB 05 stage 2 — the sealed body + idx

Stacked on #509 (`db-05c-store`), which is stacked on #494. Retarget as those land. Carries #509's object-target fix (`32e06ee`).

When a writer's frames cross `SEAL_FRAMES` (32) it folds its index into `body-<rev>.pack` + `body-<rev>.idx`; every open reads the newest body **before** the segments (so a later segment wins). Stage 1's empty `body-0.*` are now real.

## `store/body.av`

- `seal(pack) -> bool` — writes `body-<rev>.idx` then `body-<rev>.pack` (idx first, so the pack is the commit).
- The payload is §6.1's: header (magic · version · rev · compiler print) · the body's **NAMES** and interned **READ SETS** (db-names-enc's `store/names.av`, landed here) · the **CONTENT** tier (digest → bytes) · per family its **META** columns (key · value digest · set id · changed · verified). The whole payload is one commit-marked frame, so a half-written or flipped body is `torn` and read not at all.
- The **idx** is S4: a 256 fan-out (cumulative), the action keys sorted, a parallel offset each.
- `body_scan(pack)` reads `latest_body(dir)` into the pack; a torn or foreign body is ignored and says so once.

## `store/pack.av`

- `Held = { family, key, digest, read }`; `Pack.records: Cell<Map<string, Held>>` + `Pack.content` are the whole index a seal (or a compaction) copies from.
- `held()` folds a record in with the **claim law**: two digests for one action key emit `Q store claim <action-key> <digestA> <digestB>` once and keep the first (naming both writers' digests).
- The action key is now `BLAKE3(family · stamp · key)`.

## OWED, named at the site (does not ship silently)

- **`FAMILY_STAMP` is empty.** db-inputs-h's `family_code_hash` (family code hash + codec shape fingerprint) is in flight; the fold is `BLAKE3(family · stamp · key)` and the first real stamp bytes are one whole-store miss, which the per-compiler print already allows. Do not ship the empty stamp as if it were a value.
- **Compaction / gc / time-window** (db-a3-h) is the next step: fold every segment + any prior body into a new body+idx under `lock`, then sweep segments. The live set to copy is `Pack.records`/`Pack.content`; `seal_when_full` is the trigger to replace with the lock-gated step.

## `tools/store_attacks.sh` (db-measure-h)

10 attacks, **3 failure(s)** (measured on the Sprite before the seal threshold change; the code was re-run after but the Sprite's 1200 s compiler-build window cut the run):
1. `§6.8 a flipped byte (middle of a body)` — a body now exists (threshold 32) and is footer-checked; a mid-body flip is `torn`. **Not re-measured after the threshold change** — the train's runners should run it.
2. `§6.8 another compiler (a one-query rebuild)` — owed by S2's per-query code hash, not this stage.
3. `§6.8 claim conflict` — the event `Q store claim …` is implemented; the harness still fails it unconditionally until db-measure-h tests the line.

- Sprite: `pack_test` / `store_test` / `names_test` pass (the completed run showed `15/15` for the last); `make avra` builds.
- Mac: `gate_changed --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers` clean; `keepers-static` clean; `keepers-pr` clean.
- `wasm-check: all fixtures agree` for #509's object-target fix.

The tick's arm read `getpid()` on every ready-queue empty-to-non-empty
transition — twice a round trip — because the source only needs to know a
fork happened. The pid is read once per cold arm and cleared by a
`pthread_atfork` child handler, so the hot path is a compare with no
syscall and no frame before its first branch.

Stacked on #510 (`flow-03-5`): its green `runtime-tests` (the pre-existing
`late_parker` flake) and `runtime-mutations` (`the switch ignores the
tick`) are the base this needs. **Rebase onto `main` pending #510 landing**
(#510 is open, not yet queued).

## What it does

- `g_owner` is "the pid the source was armed under, or 0 when none stands
  for this process" (`runtime/host/avra_tick.c:32`). The cold arm reads
  `getpid()` once (`this_pid`, `:48`); the hot arm is
  `if (g_started && g_owner)` (`:127`, `:137`) — a compare.
- `tick_armed_cold` (`:109`, `noinline, cold`) holds the pipe/thread setup,
  so the hot path is a leaf. Disassembled: the first `sub sp`/`stp` sits
  after two branches, on the parked-wake path alone.
- `pthread_atfork(NULL, NULL, tick_after_fork)` (`:111`) registers once; the
  child handler clears `g_owner` (`:44`), so ANY fork — `avra_fiber_forked`
  or a raw `fork()` — makes the next arm replace the pipe and thread. The
  correctness the pid comparison existed for is kept.
- `tools/tick.py` allows `pthread_atfork`: registration runs on the
  scheduler's thread, never in the thread body.

## Review fixes (on the adversarial review of #523)

6. A plain `make flow-bench` prints the gate view and exits 0; only
   `FLOW_GATE=1` (`make flow-g1`) passes `--enforce` to `table.py`, so a
   FAILed row fails the gate and nothing else (`table.py`, `run.sh`).
7. `runtime-mutations` joined `KEEPERS_ALONE` beside `runtime-tests` (both
   drive clocked tests, so both stand where nothing competes for a core) —
   the mutation proof now runs on the train.
8. `flow-g1`'s skip is status 77, not 0: a machine without Go or the
   compiler reports a distinct non-success, never a pass.
9. `avra_platform.h` includes `<stdint.h>`; the header compiles alone.
10. The witness is `avra_tick_cold_pid_reads` — it counts at the `getpid()`
    call, through the arm's one reader, and names that bound.

## Tests, first

- `tick_test.c`: `the hot arm reads no process id`; `a raw fork re-arms` (no
  `avra_fiber_forked`, only the tick's own handler).
- `mutations.py`: 7 new HOST breaks — the registration, the handler body,
  the hot pid read, the owner-ignoring check, the stood-down pid read, the
  cold arm's record, and the counter. All killed; 231 of 231 total.

## MEASURED (Sprite `avra-unions-p2`, Linux x86_64, least of 5, one tree
with only `avra_tick.c` swapped)

| row | before | after | speedup | after vs Go |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ping-pong (C runtime) | 302.4 ns/rt | 92.9 ns/rt | 3.25x | — |
| spawn+join (C runtime) | 398.3 ns | 205.2 ns | 1.94x | — |

Go best: ping-pong 459.7 ns, spawn+join 742.4 ns. `getpid()` is 96 ns/call
on this Sprite. The ticket's acceptance (≤ 2x Go) holds with margin; its

On `main`, atop #517's G1 view (`tools/flow_bench/`), which it extends rather than forks.

## What it does

Ticket `avra-8sb5.34.53.32`'s acceptance. A change under `runtime/` now owes the **G1 latency gate**: the scheduler's transition rows run through the *existing* `tools/flow_bench/` harness against a recorded baseline, refusing past **2x**. `77fc7b1` (#490, "the tick") added `avra_tick_armed()` to `ready_push`'s empty edge (`runtime/avra_fiber.c:273`), whose fast path reads `getpid()` — a C gate round trip went from flow-01's 98 ns to 1059 ns, and no check ran a latency row, so it reached `main` silently.

### The mode (extend, never fork)

- `tools/flow_bench/probes/spawn_bench.c` gains one mode, `g1`: the three rows in one process, the cold parked spawn first, each the least of five. It shares `spawn1`/`joined`/`rally`/`parked` with the bench; `rally` takes its trip count so the gate can be small.
- `tools/flow_bench/run.sh --gate` builds the runtime objects and the probe through the *same* `runtime_built`/`spawn_bench` the bench uses, runs `g1` three times, and hands the raw rows to `gate.py`. No Go, no compiler, so it runs with the runtime alone.
- `tools/flow_bench/gate.py` compares to `tools/flow_bench/gate.baseline` — `<platform> <row> <total ns> <count> <toolchain>`, one row per machine like `footprint.baseline`, so a Sprite and a Mac are never compared. `make flow-gate` is the one definition; `make flow-gate-accept` re-records this machine (`FLOW_RUNTIME=<dir>` measures a runtime saved elsewhere).
- The gate always states its coverage (`N of 3 rows examined, M gated here`) and a row nobody measured is a refusal, never a pass. On a machine with no accepted row it prints the rows and does not gate; `--require` refuses instead.

**Margin 2.0x** (`FLOW_GATE_RATIO`): far above the <2% spread the rounds show, far below the ~14x one `getpid()` a transition costs.

### The rows

| row | why |
|---|---|
| `c_gate_round_trip` | the row that regressed: two `ready_push` on an empty queue, two `getpid()`. |
| `c_spawn_one` | ~2 empty-queue pushes a task — the same cost over spawn+join. |
| `c_spawn_parked_cold` | the parked transition, cold (the tick's share is smaller here). |

The **C rows** are the gate; the compiled Avra twins stay published beside Go by the G1 view (`table.py --gates`). A compiler change must not fail a runtime gate.

### Wiring

A `flow-gate` job in `.github/workflows/checks.yml`, fired by `prepare` only when the diff under `runtime/` moved (a PR, a train, or a push to main against its parent), runs `make flow-gate FLOW_GATE_ARGS=--require`; `test` aggregates it. It is deliberately not in `KEEPERS_B`: the committed baseline is the pre-tick line, so a whole-keepers train would refuse on today's `main` and this PR could not land. Once `.32`'s pid cache lands and `main` is green, adding `flow-gate` to `KEEPERS_B` is one word.

## PROBED — two runtimes through one instrument (Sprite `avra-cores`, Linux 6.12 x86_64, clang 22.1.2)

The tree's runtime (with `.32`) and a saved copy of `77fc7b1~1` (pre-tick), each recorded, each raw judged by `gate.py`:

| row | pre-tick accepted | tree (`.32`) | ratio | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `c_gate_round_trip` | 75.8 ns | 1064.2 ns | **14.03x** | REFUSE |
| `c_spawn_one` | 186.6 ns | 1204.1 ns | **6.45x** | REFUSE |
| `c_spawn_parked_cold` | 8566.0 ns | 8497.0 ns | 0.99x | pass |

- The shipped path, `make flow-gate FLOW_GATE_ARGS=--require` on the Sprite: exit 1, the two rows above named. `make` reports 2.
- The tree's own A/B (both runtimes from this tree) was 1.00x/1.06x/1.09x, exit 0 — the instrument is quiet when nothing moved.
- The Mac walks the same rows at ~82 ns a round trip (`getpid()` is free there), so no `darwin-arm64` row is accepted and the Mac prints, does not gate.

## Landing order

The committed baseline is the good (pre-tick) line, so `main` — which carries `.32` — is refused until the pid-cache fix lands. `.32`'s fix (its own runtime slice) lands first, then this gate lands green; alternatively the lead orders `make flow-gate-accept` from the tree, which blesses today's numbers (and must be re-accepted down by the fix).

## Gates

- Mac: `tools/gate_changed.sh --refs origin/main HEAD --no-keepers` clean (1 `.av` fmt-checked, #517's), `make keepers-static` exit 0.
- `make keepers-pr` on the Sprite with this tree's compiler: all six keepers exit 0 (the Mac run fails `witnesses`/`dogfooding-rules` on the stale compiler #517's report already names).
- No whole suite on a Sprite.

## Unverified

- The CI runner's `cc` string is assumed to match the Sprite's (`Ubuntu clang version 22.1.2 (1ubuntu1)`; both are `.github/ci/Dockerfile`, "as on a Sprite"). If the image's clang ever bumps, the `--require` job refuses until `run.sh --record` accepts the new toolchain's rows.
- The 2x margin was not flaked at on CI; the Sprite's rounds showed <2% spread.

DB 03c, the span/`Loc` crossing.

A `Loc` crosses as **(anchor declaration, lo offset, hi offset)**: the smallest declaration of its file whose span holds the WHOLE loc, named by `decl_wire` (its path travels with the name, so a cross-file span anchors in that file), plus each end's distance from the declaration's start. Moving the declaration moves the span with it, so an edit above changes no stored diagnostic's bytes.

**The refusal law:** a span no single declaration holds — one past its declaration's end — is REFUSED. `loc_of_wire` answers null rather than clamp a position to somewhere it never pointed. A loc with no file has no declaration to anchor in and keeps its absolute offsets.

`DiagFacts` and its `Frame`/`Suggestion`/`Edit` ride the same anchored loc.

**Verification** (the assigned Sprite `avra-bench` segfaults in the fiber scheduler for every spec suite, a known-green one included, so the native `make codecs` could not run there):
- `python3 tools/codecs.py` — 34 candidate pair(s), **36 registered, 0 acknowledged gap(s)** (was 34).

## What this does

Extends the existing flow bench (`tools/flow_bench/`) — it does not fork a
second one — with a **G1 view**: each row's Avra twin beside its Go twin on
the machine that ran, the ratio against the faster Go, and the
**2x time / 3x memory** verdict. The Avra ping-pong twin now prints the key
its Go program prints (`pingpong_rendezvous`, it is a gate rendezvous), so
the two sit on one row. Rows with no Avra twin are listed with the slice
that makes each writable.

`make flow-bench` prints the full raw table, then the G1 gate table.

## MEASURED

Sprite `avra-cores`, Linux 6.12.105-fly x86_64, 8 cpus, page 4096, go1.25.1,
**least of 5**, base `3a562c5` (runtime identical after rebase). Ratio is
against the faster Go (GOMAXPROCS=1 or default).

| G1 row | Go, 1 proc | Go, default | Avra | ratio vs best Go | gate | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ping-pong round trip (rendezvous) | 322 ns | 333 ns | 1175 ns | 3.64x | ≤ 2x | **FAIL** |
| spawn + join, one at a time | 597 ns | 609 ns | 1214 ns | 2.03x | ≤ 2x | **FAIL** |
| 10k tasks alive, cold | 1899 ns | 311 ns | 923 ns | 2.96x | ≤ 2x | **FAIL** |
| 10k tasks alive, warm | 269 ns | 196 ns | 176 ns | 0.90x | ≤ 2x | PASS |
| 10k tasks alive and parked, cold | 2574 ns | 508 ns | 8384 ns | 16.49x | ≤ 2x | **FAIL** |
| 10k tasks alive and parked, warm | 351 ns | 405 ns | 273 ns | 0.78x | ≤ 2x | PASS |
| parked bytes a task, N=1000 | 2740 B | 2904 B | 5890 B | 2.15x | ≤ 3x | PASS |
| parked bytes a task, N=30000 | 2699 B | 2716 B | 5505 B | 2.04x | ≤ 3x | PASS |
| parked bytes a task, N=100000 | 2686 B | 2672 B | 5491 B | 2.06x | ≤ 3x | PASS |
| parked bytes a task, N=500000 | 2682 B | 2669 B | 5485 B | 2.06x | ≤ 3x | PASS |

## Why the round-trip rows fail — MEASURED, not guessed

A gate round trip empties the scheduler's ready queue on each wake, and
`ready_push` calls `avra_tick_armed()` on the empty transition (added by
`77fc7b1`, #490, "the tick"). Its fast path reads `getpid()` to notice a
fork. On this Sprite **`getpid()` costs 446–453 ns** (200M calls timed out
past 180 s; 2M timed at 446.53 / 452.64 ns, twice). A round trip wakes two
parked tasks (two empty-queue pushes), so ~900 ns of the **1059 ns** C gate
round trip is `getpid()`.

- same runtime source, darwin-arm64 (Mac): **82 ns** per round trip;
- flow-01 measured **98 ns** before #490;
- `yield_switch`, which never empties the queue, is unaffected (10.3 ns
  compiled, 7.6 ns from C).

`spawn_one` (≈2 empty-queue pushes a task) and the cold parked rows carry
the same cost; `spawn_parked_cold` also carries flow-01's known
guard/page-fault cost.

**Fix candidate (runtime C — wants its own slice and an adversarial
review):** cache the pid and refresh it in a `pthread_atfork` child handler,
so the fork check costs no syscall on the hot transition.

## What cannot run yet

| G1 row | blocker |
|---|---|
| ping-pong over a buffered channel | channels — slice 05 (FLOW 05, avra-8sb5.34.53.6) |
| fan-in, N producers to one consumer | channels — slice 05 (FLOW 05, avra-8sb5.34.53.6) |
| select over N sources (2, 8, 64) | select — slice 04 (FLOW 04, avra-8sb5.34.53.4) |
| cancel a tree of tasks | cancel — slice 03 (FLOW 03, avra-8sb5.34.53.3) |

No Avra twin was faked for these; the Go-only numbers stay in the Go
columns.

## Unverified

- The ~160 ns of the C gate round trip not explained by two `getpid()`
  calls (1059 − ~900).
- 1M parked tasks: needs ~7.8 GiB, the Sprite offered 5.1 GiB free; the
  harness skipped all three engines.
- The queue-empty `avra_tick_armed()` cost was timed on this Sprite only;
  a non-virtualized Linux may have a cheaper `getpid()`, but the syscall
  remains on the hot path.
- Go was measured on the Sprite only; nothing is compared across machines.

Gates run before push: `tools/gate_changed.sh --refs origin/main HEAD
--no-keepers` and `make keepers-static` on the Mac; `make keepers-pr` on
the Sprite with this branch's compiler (the Mac copy was two commits
stale and failed `witnesses` for that reason alone).

body:
The DB05 per-record **meta** region, standalone and pure: `compiler/store/meta.av` + its suite. New module (not an extension of `names.av`) — a distinct concern, so it lands on its own. No store code, no dependency on #509.

## Layout (§6.1 `family meta`)
Column-major, one fixed width per column, the columns contiguous over the run: `action_key:32 · name_id:4 · value_digest:32 · set_id:4 · changed_at:8 · verified_at:8 · durability:1 · shape_fp:32 · code_hash:32` → **stride 153**. A record's meta is offset arithmetic from its index alone (`at + count*col_offset + i*width`), so **verification touches no value byte** — the S5 point.

## Variable-width fields: fixed slots, not name ids
The codec shape fingerprint and the producer code hash are 32-byte content digests, so they are laid out as fixed slots. A fixed slot keeps the stride constant and `span()` exact; an id into the `names` region would make a meta read depend on that region and add a lookup for nothing. (The alternative — a name-table id — is the right shape only for a field with no fixed-width carrier.)

## Entry points for the core
- `record_width() -> int` — the stride, to place `meta | values` without decoding.
- `encode_meta(rows: List<RecordMeta>) -> Bytes?` — column-major region; `null` when any digest is not exactly 32 bytes (a short slot would misalign the rest).
- `decode_meta(b: Bytes) -> Meta?` — refuses a foreign magic, a stride this module does not lay out, a region that is not a whole number of records, or a header count that disagrees with the region.
- `Meta`: `records()`, `span()` (where the values region begins), and per-index `action_key(i)`, `name_id(i)`, `value_digest(i)`, `set_id(i)`, `changed_at(i)`, `verified_at(i)`, `durability(i)`, `shape_fp(i)`, `code_hash(i)`.
- `Durability` enum (`Low`/`High`) with `RecordMeta` carrying it.

## The proof
`build/avra-try test …/store/tests/meta_test.av` → **10/10 pass**: every column round-trips, durability per record, a record read by index from a **meta-only** buffer whose length is its `span()`, and a value byte appended past the region refuses (the decoder stops exactly at meta's end). A truncated region, a region one whole record longer than its count, a foreign magic, a foreign stride, and a short digest in the encoder all refuse.

- `make keepers-static` (Mac) → exit 0. `make keepers-pr` (Sprite) → clean.

A callback under a cancel answers zero; C that follows the pointer it was handed reads the null page. The law runs before the generic seat law, so the pointer case is named for what it is.

Native claims a parked fiber (runtime/avra_fiber.c:2013) and the body runs on; the EVALUATOR skips a `legacy && virtual` park (same line) and nothing reads `avra_vtask_unwinding` on resume, so the task stays parked. # DB 05c — a second claim for one action key is reported (S7)

Stacked on #509 (`db-05c-store`, the format skeleton); **rebase onto `main`
when #509 lands**. This PR is ONE commit (`55b6427`) on top of the skeleton's
tip — the skeleton lives in the base branch, not here.

The base branch predates #505, so this commit also carries `tools/store_attacks.sh`
(from main) with the claim-conflict row un-stubbed; that file is a no-op once the
branch is rebased onto `main`.

## What

A key is an answer CLAIM (design §6.6, S7). Each writer appends its own
`seg-<pid>.log`; a reader merges every segment at open. When two segments name
DIFFERENT values for one action key, that is a reproducibility defect — the
shared store doubling as a detector of nondeterminism — so the merge REPORTS
it, naming the key, both value digests and their writers, and the later
segment's claim still stands. One line carries all of it:

    Q	store	claim-conflict	<family>	<key>	<digest-a>	<digest-b>	<seg-a>	<seg-b>

`pack.av`: `scan_segment`/`applied` thread the segment (writer) and a per-open
claim map; `claimed` records each key's first claim and reports a differing
claim from another writer. Nothing is restructured — the frame encodings, the
action table and the file layout are untouched.

`tools/store_attacks.sh`: §6.8's claim-conflict row leaves its stub. An edit
makes a second writer claim a new value for a key the first segment already
named; the reader that follows merges two disagreeing segments, its answer
still equals the cold oracle, and the report names the key, both digests and
their writers.

## Receipt (Sprite `avra-comptime`, this tree)

    store-attacks: 10 attack(s), 2 failure(s)

The claim-conflict row PASSES. The 2 remaining failures are the mechanisms
owed elsewhere, unchanged by this PR:

- a flipped byte in the middle of a body — stage 1 writes an empty
  `body-*.pack`; owed when compaction seals a body.
- another compiler, the one-query rebuild — stage 1 keys a segment by the
  compiler PRINT; needs S2's per-query code hash.

`make keepers-static` and `make inputs` green; `fmt --check` clean on the
changed `.av` with the tree's own compiler.

The one-cache/one-`obj/` host-vs-wasm object collision this lane surfaced while
gating is the skeleton's, and has been routed to its owner; it is not this
mechanism.

The DB05 encoding module, standalone and pure: `compiler/store/names.av` + its suite. It composes with `pack.av` (PR #509) through the same `@std.relation.stable` Writer/Reader codec and imports no store code, so it lands independently of the pack skeleton.

## Interface the core should call

### The name table (`Names`)
- `names() -> Names` — an empty table.
- `Names.intern(text: string) -> int` — the name's id: its position in the sorted, unique table, inserting it when absent.
- `Names.id_of(text: string) -> int?` — the id, or absence (a read, never an insert).
- `Names.text_of(id: int) -> string`
- `Names.length() -> int` — how many names the body uses (the id span).
- `Names.encode() -> Bytes` — the front-coded table: `count`, then each name as `varint(shared-prefix-bytes) + octets(suffix)`.
- `names_from(b: Bytes) -> Names?` — the table, or nothing on truncation/trailing octets/a bad prefix.

### Interned read sets (`Sets`)
- `sets() -> Sets` — an empty table.
- `Sets.intern(ids: List<int>) -> int` — the set id; members are canonicalised to rising, unique order, so `[2,1]` and `[1,2]` are one set and intern once.
- `Sets.members(id: int) -> List<int>`
- `Sets.length() -> int`
- `Sets.hash_of(id: int, rev: int) -> int` — one pure hash per set per revision (S5); every record holding the set shares the value.
- `Sets.encode() -> Bytes` — `count`, then each set as `count` + rising member ids by delta varint. Roaring would replace the deltas above the M4 size cut.
- `sets_from(b: Bytes) -> Sets?`

### Bytes it owns
`Names.encode` and `Sets.encode` are each a self-contained blob, read back by `names_from`/`sets_from` alone. The core writes them as the `names` and `sets` regions of §6.1's body (or as frames of the live segment); records then reference a `Sets` id and a `Names` id.

### The one contract to hold
`Names.intern` returns the id **at insertion**; a later name sorting earlier shifts the ids after it. So intern the body's complete name set first, then record ids — the two-pass the header layout implies. `Sets` ids never move (append-only).

## Proof
- `build/avra-try test packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/store/tests/names_test.av` — **15/15 pass**: round-trip of the table and the sets, front-coding over shared prefixes, a set interned twice gets one id, per-revision hash. Both engines: `avra test` runs it native; the suite's program tests carry their own `.expected`.
- `gate_changed --files … --packages std-avrac --no-keepers` — clean (fmt + idioms).
- `make keepers-static`, `make keepers-pr` — clean.

## What it does

The last unnamed deadlock reports now name their tasks — the naming half of G2 (`.23`).

Slice 02 landed the C case report: `case_cleared` names each task's id, spawn site, join and every filed waiter, for both a deadlock and a leak (`case_test` pins it). Two paths still said only "every task is waiting — deadlock":

- the compiled program's bare trap in `next_with_world` (`avra_fiber.c`);
- the same trap for a virtual deadlock asked outside a run.

A third — the evaluator's run (`avra_vtask_next` answering 0 while a run stands, `interp_tasks.av`'s `all_waiting()`) — returned the constant to the machine.

`deadlock_reported()` (`noinline, cold`) prints the case report's header and one line per live task, oldest first, through the SAME `task_said`/`waits_said` writers the case report uses: `task N, spawned at <site>, joins task M` / `waits on gate 0x` / `waits on descriptor N` / `waits on a time`. `main` is named first in a compiled run (it is static, not on `g_all`, as the door listing already knows). Ids are the process's (`id_of`), not the case's relative ones. No heap allocation — stderr only — so it is legal on `avra_trap`'s cold path. Called before the compiled trap and on the evaluator's 0 answer; no new runtime row, so no declaration ladder.

The evaluator's failure string (`all_waiting()`) is unchanged; the names ride stderr, as the native case's do.

## MEASURED vs ESTIMATE

```

  task 0, the program's own run, joins task 1
  task 1, spawned at 0x102c4d1a0, waits on gate 0x7f8e0c010

```

`a sleep and a reader among yielding tasks wake within reach` and the tick window (`flow_test`, `tick_test`) stay green.

rung 1 of ladder 5 (flow-03 §3.3): the shield's runtime half. No `rt_sigs`
row, no Avra declaration, no compiler change — ladder 6 rungs them.

## What it does

- `avra_fiber_shield_enter`/`_leave` (and the vtask twins): the enter saves
  the task's unwind bit and clears it, so a call that may reach is not cut
  between the deferred calls; the leave ORs the saved bit back. A nested
  bracket is a depth, so a deferred call's own cold exit nests.
- `Fiber.shield_depth`/`shield_saved`; `Scope.shield`, set by
  `within_opened` from the running task's depth.
- A SHIELD SCOPE: `cancel_stands`, `park_begun`, `fiber_cancelled` and
  `deadline_reached` let a `within` opened while shielded answer ONLY its own
  limit, never the task's cancel (CHANNELS §5.4 law 10).
- A checked back-edge in a shielded task yields and raises nothing.

## Review fixes (this push, on the independent review of #510)

1. **HIGH — the leave ORs** (`runtime/avra_fiber.c:2173`). The old
   `*bit = f->shield_saved` erased a `cancel_met()` raised by a wait inside
   the shield when the saved bit was 0, so `fiber_start` wrote `END_ANSWERED`.
   Witness `a_cancel_met_inside_a_shield_survives` (a cancelled task whose
   shield holds a cut wait ends cancelled, the bit standing); the nested
   test's final assertion now asserts the bit stands (`g_byte_d == 1`) and
   the task unwinds.
2. **HIGH — the flake is gone.** `late_parker_after_interrupt`'s second half
   spun on the wall clock, which the scheduler never observed, then yielded
   before the deadline was read: 3–4 of 6 red on the unmodified branch.
   It now `avra_fiber_sleep(6)`s past the waiter's 3 ms deadline, so the
   deadline fires under an idle queue. 10/10 green.
3. **LOW** — `scope_inherited` uses a designated
   `(Scope){ .id = …, .at = …, .first = 0, .shield = 0 }`; the mutation's
   text follows.
4. **MEDIUM — the vtask byte pair is no longer a no-op.** Landed the
   evaluator's setter `avra_vtask_set_unwinding` (`avra_fiber.c:2343`),
   witnessed by `shield_bytes` (vtask_test): the enter clears a set bit, the
   leave keeps a bit raised inside. The vtask scope mirror (`shields`) still
   holds.
5. **MEDIUM — OWED, recorded.** "No exit path leaks a shield" (a trap
   mid-defer, a fork taken there, an unbalanced frame) is unwitnessable until
   ladder 9 emits the bracket; recorded in
   `docs/2026_10_08_FLOW_03_LADDER5.md` with that trigger.

## Also fixed

`the switch ignores the tick` was a mutation that SURVIVED on main: the
existing tick test files a timer, which zeroes the poller countdown, so the
tick-set `queue_alone` path was never taken with the countdown still
standing. `tick_test`'s `a tick forces the switch through the world` (a
ready task, the countdown long, the tick held) kills it.

## Tests, first

- `flow_test.c`: save/clear/restore; the cancel-met-inside witness; nesting;
  a shielded back-edge; the shield-scope wait/sleep/cancel cases.
- `vtask_test.c`: the byte pair (`shield_bytes`) and the scope mirror
  (`shields`).
- `tick_test.c`: the tick forces the world path.
- `mutations.py`: a break per new/changed line.

## MEASURED

- `make runtime-tests`: 0 failed (Sprite, Linux x86_64).
- `make runtime-mutations`: 224 of 224 killed, 0 survived, 0 rotten.
- `make keepers` WHOLE (Sprite): every keeper, exit 0.

## Unverified / follow-ups

- The compiler half is ladder 9: emitting the bracket on a frame's cold
  exit, dropping the "call that may reach" test inside it, and
  `flow.unbounded_cleanup`.
- No `rt_sigs` row / Avra declaration / evaluator arm yet (ladder 6); the
  vtask setter lands ahead of its evaluator caller.
- A `defer` whose wait is a plain `sleep` under a shield scope is not cut by
  the cancel, but not yet by the `within`'s limit either (ladder 14).
- The Mac-only `keepers-pr` refusal is a stale Mac compiler (the same

DB 05 acceptance half (design §6.8), tools/ only. Owns `tools/store_attacks.sh` and `tools/store_baseline.sh`.

The store is now a DIRECTORY (design §6.1), one per tree for every compiler (S2): `.avra-cache/store/` holds `body-<rev>.pack`, `body-<rev>.idx`, `seg-<writer>.log` and `lock`, beside `.avra-cache/obj/` and `.avra-cache/bin/`. The old script wanted `store` to be a FILE under `.avra-cache/*/`. Every §6.8 attack is preserved and the summary line is unchanged. Each check names the row it enforces; an attack the directory shape changes names its mapping, and one stage 1 cannot satisfy FAILS by name rather than passing vacuously.

Mappings the directory shape changed:
- one store: `ls .avra-cache` is `store obj bin`, and `store/` is a directory carrying `lock`.
- two writers vs compaction contended: the old script folded both into one two-at-once check; they are now two checks (S7: writers own segments, no lock; the flock is compaction's alone).
- a flipped byte — the two file-specific cases: a byte in a live `seg-<writer>.log` last frame, and a byte in a sealed `body-*.pack`.
- another compiler: the segment's plain header print, not the one store file's.

Run against db-store-h's stage-1 skeleton (avra-comptime, Linux), `sh tools/store_attacks.sh`:

    store-attacks: 10 attack(s), 3 failure(s)

Passing: one store · one open · a warm edit seen (S5) · kill mid-append · two writers (two segments) · compaction contended (skipped named) · flipped byte in the live segment · another compiler (foreign header refused).

The 3 failures name the owed mechanisms, not defects in the script:
- flipped byte (middle of a body): stage 1 writes an empty `body-*.pack` — the attack is owed when compaction seals a body.
- another compiler, the one-query rebuild: stage 1 keys a segment by the compiler PRINT, so a rebuild that changed one query is a whole-store miss; the per-query recompute needs S2's query code hash.
- a claim conflict: no check/event when two segments hold different digests for one action key — a line naming the key and the two digests is owed.

Events and hooks used (all present in the stage-1 skeleton): `Q store open/skipped/torn/foreign`, `AVRA_STORE_KILL=commit`, `AVRA_STORE_HOLD_MS=n`. The harness sets `AVRA_WATCH_HELD=1` so two writers and a contended compaction run concurrently rather than serialising on the shim's package lock (same door as `tools/cache_attacks.sh` and the baseline).

`tools/store_baseline.sh` reports files and bytes per store part (`body-*.pack`, `body-*.idx`, `seg-*.log`, `lock`, `obj/`, `bin/`) instead of the old per-compiler per-family walk.

Its recursion cut is PATH-DEPENDENT — `shape_in` emits `rec ${open.index_of(seen.index)}` — so a per-TypeId settle-always memo is unsound, and the abandon rule that keeps it correct is exactly why it cannot pay. Tracked in `avra-jvf4`; cross-links `avra-8sb5.57.172`.
